title.zh: 卷一百八十二 列傳第一百零七 二李崔蕭二鄭視盧韋周二裴劉趙王
title.en: Volume 182 Biographies 107: Two Li's, Cui, Xiao, Two Zhengs, Shi, Liu, Wei, Zhou, Two Pei's, Liu, Zhao, Wang
title.raw: 卷一百八十二 列傳第一百零七 二李崔蕭二鄭視盧韋周二裴劉趙王 Volume 182 Biographies 107: Two Li's, Cui, Xiao, Two Zhengs, Shi, Liu, Wei, Zhou, Two Pei's, Liu, Zhao, Wang

sentences.zh: 二李崔蕭二鄭二盧韋周二裴劉趙王

translations.literal: Two Lis, Cui, Xiao, two Zhengs, two Lus, Wei, Zhou, two Peis, Liu, Zhao, Wang
translations.idiomatic: The Two Lis, Cui, Xiao, the Two Zhengs, the Two Lus, Wei, Zhou, the Two Peis, Liu, Zhao, and Wang

sentences.zh: 李固言，字仲樞，其先趙人。

translations.literal: Li Guyán, styled Zhòngshū, his ancestors were men of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guyán, courtesy name Zhòngshū, came from a Zhao family.

sentences.zh: 擢進士甲科，江西裴堪、劍南王播皆表署幕府。

translations.literal: He was selected in the first rank of jinshi graduates; both Pei Kān of Jiangxi and Wáng Bō of Jiannan memorialized to appoint him to their staff offices.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the top class, and both Pei Kān in Jiangxi and Wáng Bō in Jiannan recommended him for posts on their staffs.

sentences.zh: 累官戶部郎中。

translations.literal: Through successive offices he reached Langzhong of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to become a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 溫造為御史中丞，表知雜事，進給事中。

translations.literal: When Wēn Zào served as Vice Censor-in-Chief, he memorialized that Guyán should handle miscellaneous business, and Guyán was advanced to Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wēn Zào was vice censor-in-chief, he recommended Guyán to handle routine business and had him promoted to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 將作監王堪坐治太廟不謹，改太子賓客，固言上還制書曰：「陛下當以名臣左右太子，堪以慢官斥，處調護地非所宜。」

translations.literal: Director of Palace Buildings Wáng Kān, having been charged with careless management of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, was reassigned as Mentor of the Heir Apparent. Guyán returned the edict and said: "Your Majesty ought to place renowned ministers at the heir's side. Kān was dismissed for neglect of office; a post of nurture and protection is not suitable for him."
translations.idiomatic: Wáng Kān, director of palace construction, was demoted for mismanaging the ancestral temple and made mentor to the crown prince. Guyán returned the edict, writing: "Your Majesty should surround the heir with eminent ministers. Kān was removed for dereliction; a nurturing post is no fit place for him."

sentences.zh: 詔改它王傅。

translations.literal: An edict ordered another man appointed tutor to the king.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered someone else appointed crown prince tutor.

sentences.zh: 固言再遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Guyán was again transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guyán was soon promoted again to right vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 李德裕輔政，出固言華州刺史。

translations.literal: When Lǐ Déyù directed the government, Guyán was sent out as governor of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: While Lǐ Déyù held power, Guyán was posted out as governor of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 俄而李宗閔復用，召為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long Lǐ Zōngmǐn was restored to favor and summoned Guyán back as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Lǐ Zōngmǐn returned to power and recalled him as vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 州大豪何延慶橫猾，嘩眾遮道，使不得去，固言怒，捕取杖殺之，屍諸道。

translations.literal: A great bully of the prefecture, Hé Yánqìng, was violent and cunning; he stirred a crowd to block the road so the envoy could not leave. Guyán in anger seized him, beat him to death with the staff, and displayed the corpse along the road.
translations.idiomatic: A local magnate, Hé Yánqìng, ruled by force and fraud; he roused a mob to bar the road and keep the new governor from departing. Guyán had him seized, beaten to death, and his body displayed along the highway.

sentences.zh: 既領選，按籍自擬，先收寒素，柅吏奸。

translations.literal: Once he took charge of selection, he examined the registers himself, first enrolling men of humble origin and restraining clerical corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Once in charge of appointments, he reviewed the registers himself, giving priority to candidates of modest background and curbing graft among the clerks.

sentences.zh: 進御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 太和九年，宗閔得罪，李訓、鄭註用事，訓欲自取宰相，乃先以固言為門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taihe, Zōngmǐn fell from grace; Lǐ Xùn and Zhèng Zhù held power. Xùn wished to take the chancellorship himself, and so first made Guyán Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs with the Grand Councilor title.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 9, Zōngmǐn was disgraced and Lǐ Xùn and Zhèng Zhù took control. Xùn wanted the chancellorship for himself, so he first installed Guyán as vice director of the Chancellery and grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 旋坐黨人，出為山南西道節度使，訓自代其處。

translations.literal: Shortly he was implicated as a partisan and sent out as military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit; Xùn himself replaced him in that post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon banished as a factional ally and made military commissioner of Shannan West, while Xùn took his place.

sentences.zh: 訓敗，文宗頗思之，復召為平章事，仍判戶部。

translations.literal: When Xùn fell, Emperor Wénzōng thought much of Guyán and recalled him as Grand Councilor, still overseeing the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After Xùn's downfall, Emperor Wénzōng missed him and recalled him as grand councilor, with continued charge of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 群臣請上徽號，帝曰：「今治道猶郁，群臣之請謂何？

translations.literal: The ministers asked that a honorific title be bestowed. The emperor said: "The way of governance is still troubled—what do the ministers' request mean?
translations.idiomatic: The court asked that an honorific epithet be conferred. The emperor said: "The realm is still unsettled—what is the point of your petition?

sentences.zh: 比州縣多不治，信乎？」

translations.literal: Of late many prefectures and counties are ill governed—is that true?"
translations.idiomatic: Is it true that so many prefectures and counties are poorly governed lately?"

sentences.zh: 固言因白鄧州刺史王堪、隋州刺史鄭襄尤無狀。

translations.literal: Guyán thereupon reported that Dèng Prefecture governor Wáng Kān and Suí Prefecture governor Zhèng Xiāng were especially unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Guyán then named Dèngzhou governor Wáng Kān and Suízhou governor Zhèng Xiāng as especially incompetent.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「貞元時御史，獨王堪爾。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In the Zhenyuan era among censors, only Wáng Kān."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "In the Zhenyuan reign, among censors there was only Wáng Kān."

sentences.zh: 鄭覃本舉堪，疑固言抵己，即曰：「臣知堪，故用為刺史。

translations.literal: Zhèng Tán had originally recommended Kān and suspected Guyán was attacking him, and at once said: "Your servant knew Kān and therefore appointed him prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Zhèng Tán, who had recommended Kān, suspected a personal attack and replied: "I knew Kān well, which is why I made him prefect.

sentences.zh: 舉天下不職，何獨二人？」

translations.literal: Throughout the realm who is not derelict—why only these two men?"
translations.idiomatic: Neglect is everywhere under heaven—why single out these two?"

sentences.zh: 帝識其意，不主前語，因稱：「《詩》曰『濟濟多士，文王以寧。』

translations.literal: The emperor perceived his intent and did not uphold his earlier words, and therefore said: "The Odes say, 'With many officers in array, King Wen had peace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw his point, set aside his earlier remark, and said: "The Book of Songs says, 'With officers thronging, King Wen knew peace.

sentences.zh: 聞德宗時多闕官，寧乏才邪？」

translations.literal: I have heard that in Emperor Dézōng's time many offices stood vacant—can there truly be a lack of talent?"
translations.idiomatic: I hear that under Dézōng many posts went unfilled—can talent really be so scarce?"

sentences.zh: 固言曰：「用人之道，隨所保任，觀稱與否而升黜之，無乏才矣。」

translations.literal: Guyán said: "The way to employ men is to follow those whom one vouches for, observe whether they win praise or not, and promote or demote accordingly—then there will be no lack of talent."
translations.idiomatic: Guyán said: "The art of appointment is to stand behind those you recommend, watch whether they earn praise, and promote or remove them accordingly—then talent will never run short."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「宰相用人毋計親疏。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When grand councilors employ men, do not reckon closeness or distance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "In appointing men, a chancellor must not weigh kinship.

sentences.zh: 竇易直為宰相，未嘗用姻戚。

translations.literal: Dòu Yìzhí as grand councilor never employed affinal kin.
translations.idiomatic: Dòu Yìzhí, as chancellor, never favored his in-laws.

sentences.zh: 使己才不足任天下重，自宜引去；

translations.literal: If one's own talent is insufficient to bear the weight of all under Heaven, one ought of oneself to withdraw;
translations.idiomatic: If one's own ability cannot bear the empire's burden, one should step down;

sentences.zh: 茍公舉，雖親何嫌？

translations.literal: if the recommendation is public, what scruple though the man be kin?
translations.idiomatic: but if the nomination is merit-based, what harm if the man is a relative?

sentences.zh: 用所長耳！」

translations.literal: One uses what he excels at, that is all!"
translations.idiomatic: One simply employs his strengths!"

sentences.zh: 帝不欲大臣有黨，故語兩與之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not wish great ministers to form factions, and therefore spoke to both of them in this way.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, wishing to discourage faction among his ministers, addressed them both in these terms.

sentences.zh: 俄以門下侍郎平章事為西川節度使，詔雲韶雅樂即臨臯館送之。

translations.literal: Shortly, from Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor he became military commissioner of Xichuan; an edict ordered the elegant music of the Cloud Suite played at Lingao Pavilion to send him off.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent from the chancellery to serve as military commissioner of Xichuan, with court musicians ordered to perform at Lingao Pavilion for his farewell.

sentences.zh: 讓還門下侍郎，乃檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He declined and returned to Vice Director of the Chancellery, then was made acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He declined and resumed the vice chancellorship, then received the acting post of left vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 始置騾軍千匹，又募銳士三千，武備雄完。

translations.literal: He first established a mule corps of a thousand beasts, and also recruited three thousand crack troops; military preparations were strong and complete.
translations.idiomatic: He raised a thousand-pack mule train and recruited three thousand elite troops, bringing the command's defenses to full strength.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，召授右僕射。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wǔzōng acceded, Guyán was summoned and appointed Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wǔzōng took the throne, Guyán was recalled as right vice director.

sentences.zh: 會崔珙、陳夷行以僕射為宰相，改檢校司空兼太子少師，領河中節度使。

translations.literal: It happened that Cuī Gǒng and Chén Yíxíng became grand councilors while holding the vice directorship, so Guyán was changed to acting Minister of Works with concurrent office as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and took charge as military commissioner of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Cuī Gǒng and Chén Yíxíng became chancellors while still vice directors, Guyán was reassigned as acting minister of works and junior tutor to the heir, with command of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 蒲津歲河水壞梁，吏撤笮用舟，邀丐行人。

translations.literal: Each year at Pujin the Yellow River destroyed the bridge; clerks removed the pontoon and used boats, waylaying travelers to beg.
translations.idiomatic: At Pujin the Yellow River annually wrecked the bridge; officials dismantled the pontoon, ferried travelers by boat, and extorted tolls from them.

sentences.zh: 固言至，悉除之。

translations.literal: When Guyán arrived, he abolished all of this.
translations.idiomatic: Guyán abolished the practice entirely on taking office.

sentences.zh: 帝伐回鶻，詔方鎮獻財助軍，上疏固諫，不從。

translations.literal: The emperor campaigned against the Uyghurs and ordered the regional commands to offer wealth to aid the army; Guyán memorialized firmly in remonstrance, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched against the Uyghurs and ordered the provinces to contribute funds, Guyán submitted a strong protest, but the court would not listen.

sentences.zh: 以疾復為少師，遷東都留守。

translations.literal: On account of illness he again became Junior Tutor and was transferred to be Protector of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Illness led to his reassignment as junior tutor and protector of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初，還右僕射。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuānzōng's reign he returned as Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuānzōng's reign he was restored as right vice director.

sentences.zh: 後以太子太傅分司東都。

translations.literal: Later he served as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent with detached duty at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He later held the title of grand tutor to the heir while on detached duty in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十八，贈太尉。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-eight and was posthumously given Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-eight and was posthumously honored as grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 固言吃，接賓客頗謇緩，然每議論人主前，乃更詳辯。

translations.literal: Guyán stammered and received guests in a rather halting and slow manner, yet whenever he discussed matters before the sovereign he became all the more detailed and eloquent.
translations.idiomatic: Guyán had a stammer and was rather slow and stiff with guests, yet in debate before the throne he grew notably fluent and precise.

sentences.zh: 李玨，字待價，其先出趙郡，客居淮陰。

translations.literal: Lǐ Jué, styled Dàijià, his forebears came from Zhao commandery and lived as sojourners in Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Lǐ Jué, courtesy name Dàijià, was of Zhao commandery ancestry but had settled in Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he served his mother and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Left fatherless early, he won renown for devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 甫冠，舉明經。

translations.literal: Just upon coming of age he passed the Mingjing examination.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after reaching manhood he passed the classics examination.

sentences.zh: 李絳為華州刺史，見之，曰：「日角珠廷，非庸人相。

translations.literal: When Lǐ Jiàng was governor of Huazhou and saw him, he said: "Sun-corner brow and pearl forehead—this is not the countenance of a mediocre man.
translations.idiomatic: Lǐ Jiàng, then governor of Huazhou, met him and said: "With a brow like the sun and a jeweled forehead, you are no ordinary face.

sentences.zh: 明經碌碌，非子所宜。」

translations.literal: The Mingjing path is a mediocre track—not what suits you."
translations.idiomatic: The classics degree is a pedestrian road—not for you."

sentences.zh: 乃更舉進士高第。

translations.literal: He then took the jinshi examination again and placed in the top rank.
translations.idiomatic: Jué then sat for the jinshi and graduated with highest honors.

sentences.zh: 河陽烏重胤表置幕府。

translations.literal: Wū Zhòngyǐn of Heyang memorialized to place him on the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Wū Zhòngyǐn of Heyang recommended him for a staff post.

sentences.zh: 以拔萃補渭南尉，擢右拾遺。

translations.literal: Through exceptional selection he was appointed Wei of Weinan, then promoted to Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Selected on merit, he became magistrate of Weinan and was then raised to right reminder.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵使王播增茶稅十之五以佐用度。

translations.literal: Salt and Iron Commissioner Wáng Bō increased the tea tax by five-tenths to supplement expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: Wáng Bō, commissioner of salt and iron, raised the tea levy by half again to cover expenses.

sentences.zh: 玨上疏謂：「榷率本濟軍興，而稅茶自貞元以來有之。

translations.literal: Jué memorialized, saying: "Monopoly rates were originally to aid military campaigns, and the tea tax has existed since the Zhenyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: Jué submitted a memorial arguing: "State monopolies were meant to fund armies, and the tea tax has stood since Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 方天下無事，忽厚斂以傷國體，一不可。

translations.literal: Now when all under Heaven is without trouble, suddenly to levy heavily and injure the body politic—first, this must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm is at peace, a sudden heavy levy wounds the state—this is unacceptable for one reason.

sentences.zh: 茗為人飲，與鹽粟同資，若重稅之，售必高，其敝先及貧下，二不可。

translations.literal: Tea is what people drink, a staple like salt and grain; if heavily taxed, the price of sale must rise, and the harm will first reach the poor—second, this must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Tea is a daily drink, as essential as salt and grain; heavier taxes will raise prices and hurt the poor first—a second reason to refuse.

sentences.zh: 山澤之產無定數，程斤論稅，以售多為利，若價騰踴，則市者稀，其稅幾何？

translations.literal: Products of mountains and marshes have no fixed quantity; taxing by measured weight takes profit from high sales—if prices soar, buyers will be few; how much revenue will there be?
translations.idiomatic: Harvests from hill and marsh are uncertain; taxing by weight assumes volume brings profit—yet if prices spike, buyers vanish and revenue with them—a third objection.

sentences.zh: 三不可。

translations.literal: Third, this must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: For a third reason, it must not be done.

sentences.zh: 陛下初即位，詔懲聚斂，今反增茶賦，必失人心。」

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first took the throne, an edict punished hoarding and exaction; now to increase the tea levy instead will surely lose the people's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: At your accession you vowed to punish extortion; to raise the tea tax now will surely cost you the people's trust."

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected the advice.

sentences.zh: 方是時，禁中造百尺樓，土木費鉅萬，故播亟斂，陰中帝欲。

translations.literal: At this time within the palace a hundred-foot tower was built; earthworks and timber cost tens of thousands, and so Bō urgently levied collections, secretly aligning with the emperor's desires.
translations.idiomatic: The palace was then building a hundred-foot tower at vast cost, so Bō rushed to raise funds and quietly played to the emperor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 玨以數諫不得留，出為下邽令。

translations.literal: Jué, because he remonstrated repeatedly and could not remain, was sent out as magistrate of Xiagui.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated remonstrance left him unwelcome at court, Jué was posted out as magistrate of Xiagui.

sentences.zh: 武昌牛僧孺辟署掌書記，還為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Niú Sēnglú of Wuchang summoned him to serve as chief secretary; he returned and became Attending Censor within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Niú Sēnglú at Wuchang made him chief secretary; he later returned to the capital as palace attending censor.

sentences.zh: 宰相韋處厚曰：「清廟之器，豈擊搏才乎？」

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Wéi Chùhòu said: "A vessel for the pure temple—how could he be talent for striking and wrestling?"
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Wéi Chùhòu said: "He is fit for the ancestral temple, not for rough work."

sentences.zh: 除禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Jué was appointed an outer gentleman in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 僧孺還相，以司勛員外郎知制誥為翰林學士，加戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Sēnglú returned as chancellor, Jué, as Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel with charge of drafting edicts, became Hanlin Academician and was given the additional title of Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Sēnglú returned as chancellor, Jué became a Hanlin academician drafting edicts and was made vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 始，鄭註以醫進，文宗一日語玨曰：「卿亦知有鄭註乎？

translations.literal: At the beginning Zhèng Zhù advanced through medicine; one day Emperor Wénzōng said to Jué: "Do you also know there is a Zhèng Zhù?
translations.idiomatic: Zhèng Zhù had risen as a physician; one day Wénzōng asked Jué: "Have you heard of Zhèng Zhù?

sentences.zh: 宜與之言。」

translations.literal: You ought to speak with him."
translations.idiomatic: You should speak with him."

sentences.zh: 玨曰：「臣知之，奸回人也。」

translations.literal: Jué said: "Your servant knows him—a treacherous and perverse man."
translations.idiomatic: Jué replied: "I know him, Your Majesty—a devious man."

sentences.zh: 帝愕然曰：「朕疾愈，註力也。

translations.literal: The emperor started and said: "My illness was cured—Zhù's effort.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was taken aback: "My recovery was Zhù's doing.

sentences.zh: 可不一見之？」

translations.literal: Can you not meet him once?"
translations.idiomatic: Will you not at least meet him?"

sentences.zh: 註由是怨玨。

translations.literal: From this Zhù bore resentment toward Jué.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Zhù bore Jué a grudge.

sentences.zh: 及李宗閔以罪去，玨為申辨，貶江州刺史。

translations.literal: When Lǐ Zōngmǐn left office through crime, Jué spoke in his defense and was demoted to governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zōngmǐn fell, Jué spoke in his defense and was banished to Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 徙河南尹，復為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Mayor of Henan and again became Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to mayor of Henan and restored as vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 開成中，楊嗣復得君，引玨同中書門下平章事，與李固言皆善。

translations.literal: In the Kaicheng era Yáng Sìfù gained the ruler's trust and brought Jué in as Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs with the Grand Councilor title; he was on good terms with Lǐ Guyán.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaicheng, Yáng Sìfù won the emperor's favor and made Jué grand councilor; he and Li Guyán were close allies.

sentences.zh: 三人者居中秉權，乃與鄭覃、陳夷行等更持議，一好惡，相影和，朋黨益熾矣。

translations.literal: The three men held power at the center, and then with Zhèng Tán, Chén Yíxíng, and others they took turns in debate, unified in likes and dislikes, echoing one another—factionalism grew all the fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: The three held the center of power; they and rivals such as Zhèng Tán and Chén Yíxíng traded arguments in lockstep blocs, and court factions burned hotter than ever.

sentences.zh: 玨數辭位，不許。

translations.literal: Jué several times resigned his post and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jué repeatedly tried to resign, but the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗自謂：「臨天下十四年，雖未至治，然視今日承平亦希矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor once said of himself: "I have faced all under Heaven for fourteen years; though we have not reached perfect order, yet compared with today's peace, how rare that is!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said: "I have ruled fourteen years; we are not yet in full order, but peace like today's is rare!"

sentences.zh: 玨曰：「為國者如治身，及身康寧，調適以自助，如恃安而忽，則疾生。

translations.literal: Jué said: "Governing a state is like tending the body: when the body is sound, one regulates and adjusts to aid oneself; if one relies on safety and neglects care, illness arises.
translations.idiomatic: Jué said: "Governing a state is like caring for the body: when you are well, you must still regulate your habits; if you trust ease and grow careless, sickness follows.

sentences.zh: 天下當無事，思所闕，禍亂可至哉？」

translations.literal: When all under Heaven should be without trouble, think on what is lacking—can calamity and disorder be far?"
translations.idiomatic: When the realm seems untroubled, consider what is missing—disaster may be closer than you think."

sentences.zh: 杜悰領度支有勞，帝欲拜戶部尚書，以問宰相。

translations.literal: Dù Zōng, who headed the Directorate of Public Revenue, had merit; the emperor wished to appoint him Minister of Revenue and asked the grand councilors.
translations.idiomatic: Dù Zōng had distinguished service at the revenue directorate, and the emperor wished to make him minister of revenue and asked the chancellors.

sentences.zh: 陳夷行答曰：「恩權予奪，願陛下自斷。」

translations.literal: Chén Yíxíng answered: "Grace and authority to grant or withdraw—may Your Majesty decide for himself."
translations.idiomatic: Chén Yíxíng answered: "Favor and power are yours to give or withhold; let Your Majesty decide alone."

sentences.zh: 玨曰：「祖宗倚宰相，天下事皆先平章，故官曰平章事。

translations.literal: Jué said: "The ancestral emperors relied on grand councilors; all affairs under Heaven were first deliberated by the Grand Councilors—hence the office is called 'Associate Director of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jué said: "Our forebears relied on chancellors; state business was settled by the council first—hence the title 'grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 君臣相須，所以致太平也。

translations.literal: Ruler and minister depend on each other—by this peace is brought about.
translations.idiomatic: Sovereign and minister need one another; that is how peace is achieved.

sentences.zh: 茍用一吏、處一事皆決於上，將焉用彼相哉？

translations.literal: If employing one clerk or handling one matter all are decided above, of what use are those councilors?
translations.idiomatic: If every clerk and every affair is settled only by the throne, what need is there for chancellors?

sentences.zh: 隋文帝勞於小務，以疑待下，故二世而亡。

translations.literal: Emperor Wén of Sui toiled over petty tasks and treated subordinates with suspicion, and therefore his line perished in the second generation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wén of Sui wore himself on trifles and met his officials with suspicion, and his house fell in the second generation.

sentences.zh: 陛下嘗謂臣曰：『竇易直勸我，凡宰相啟擬，五取三，二取一。

translations.literal: Your Majesty once told your servant: 'Dòu Yìzhí advised me that of all memorial proposals from grand councilors, take three from five and one from two.'
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty once told me: 'Dòu Yìzhí urged that of every five chancellor nominations I should accept three, and of every two, one.'

sentences.zh: 彼宜勸我擇宰相，不容勸我疑宰相。』」

translations.literal: He ought to have urged me to choose grand councilors, not permitted to urge me to suspect grand councilors.'
translations.idiomatic: He should have helped me choose chancellors, not taught me to distrust them.'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「易直此言殊可鄙。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yìzhí's words are truly contemptible."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That advice of Yìzhí's was truly base."

sentences.zh: 帝又語：「貞元初政事誠善。」

translations.literal: The emperor spoke again: "In early Zhenyuan governance was truly good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor added: "Early Zhenyuan administration was indeed sound."

sentences.zh: 玨曰：「德宗晚喜聚財，方鎮以進奉市恩，吏得賦外求索，此其敝也。」

translations.literal: Jué said: "In his later years Dézōng delighted in amassing wealth; regional commands used tribute submissions to buy favor, and clerks could seek beyond the tax rolls—this was its flaw."
translations.idiomatic: Jué said: "Late in his reign Dézōng loved hoarding wealth; provinces bought favor with tribute, and officials preyed beyond the tax rolls—that was its flaw."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「人君輕所賦，節所用，可乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "For a ruler to lighten what is levied and economize what is spent—would that do?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "Would it suffice for a ruler to levy lightly and spend sparingly?"

sentences.zh: 玨曰：「貞觀時，房、杜、王、魏為文皇帝謀，固此耳！」

translations.literal: Jué said: "In the Zhenguan era Fáng, Dù, Wáng, and Wèi counseled Emperor Wén—solidly this!"
translations.idiomatic: Jué said: "In Zhenguan, Fáng, Dù, Wáng, and Wèi advised Taizong—precisely on this point!"

sentences.zh: 帝頗向納。

translations.literal: The emperor was quite inclined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was much persuaded.

sentences.zh: 進封贊皇縣男。

translations.literal: He was advanced in enfeoffment to Baron of Zanhuang county.
translations.idiomatic: He was ennobled as baron of Zanhuang county.

sentences.zh: 宣宗立，內徙郴、舒二州，以太子賓客分司東都。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuānzōng acceded, Jué was moved within the realm to Chén and Shū prefectures, then served as Guest of the Heir Apparent with detached duty at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuānzōng came to the throne, Jué was shifted inland to Chén and Shū, then served as guest of the heir on detached duty in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 遷河陽節度使，罷橫賦宿逋百餘萬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner of Heyang and abolished illegal levies and long-standing arrears totaling more than a million.
translations.idiomatic: As military commissioner of Heyang he abolished illegal surcharges and cleared more than a million in old arrears.

sentences.zh: 以吏部尚書召，玨去鎮，而府庫十倍於初。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Personnel; when Jué left the command, the treasury was tenfold what it had been at the start.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as minister of personnel, he left the command with the treasury ten times fuller than when he arrived.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校尚書右僕射、淮南節度使。

translations.literal: Shortly he was made acting Right Vice Director and military commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting right vice director and military commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 玨顧己大臣，誼不以內外自異，表請立皇太子維天下心。

translations.literal: Jué, mindful that he was a great minister and that propriety did not distinguish inner from outer, memorialized asking that the crown prince be established to steady the hearts of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of his rank as a senior minister and that duty did not change inside or outside the capital, he memorialized to establish a crown prince and steady the realm.

sentences.zh: 江淮旱，發倉廩賑流民，以軍羨儲殺半價與人。

translations.literal: The Jiang-Huai region suffered drought; he opened granaries to relieve wandering people and sold grain from military surplus stores at half price to the populace.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck the Jiang-Huai region, he opened the granaries to aid refugees and sold army reserve grain to the people at half price.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十九，贈司空，謚曰貞穆。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-nine; posthumously he was made Minister of Works, with posthumous title Zhenmu.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-nine and was posthumously honored as minister of works with the epithet Zhenmu, "Upright and Solemn."

sentences.zh: 始，淮南三節度皆卒於鎮，人勸易署寢，玨曰：「上命我守揚州，是實正寢，若何去之？」

translations.literal: At the outset, all three Huainan military commissioners had died in their commands; people urged him to change the official residence. Jué said: "The emperor ordered me to guard Yangzhou—this is truly the proper chamber; why should I leave it?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, each of three successive Huainan commissioners had died in office, and his staff urged him to move to another residence. Jué said: "The throne ordered me to hold Yangzhou; this room is the rightful one—why should I abandon it?"

sentences.zh: 及疾亟，官屬見臥內，惟以州有稅酒直而神策軍常為豪商占利，方論奏，未見報為恨，一不及家事。

translations.literal: When his illness grew critical, subordinates who saw him in his bedchamber found that he spoke only of how the prefecture had wine-tax revenue yet the Shence Army constantly monopolized the profit for great merchants; he was in the midst of memorializing and regretted that no reply had come—not one word touched family affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened, those who attended him in his chamber heard him speak only of wine-tax revenue in the prefecture that the Shence Army habitually seized for powerful merchants; he was still pressing a memorial on the matter and grieved that no answer had come—not once did he mention his household.

sentences.zh: 性寡欲，早喪妻，不置妾侍，門無饋餉。

translations.literal: By nature he had few desires; he lost his wife early, kept no concubines, and no gifts came to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: He lived simply, was widowed young, kept no concubines, and accepted no presents at his door.

sentences.zh: 淮南之人德之，玨已歿，叩闕下，願立碑刻其遺愛雲。

translations.literal: The people of Huainan were grateful to him; after Jué had died they came to the palace gates and asked to erect a stele inscribing his lingering kindness.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Huainan revered him; after his death they petitioned at the palace to raise a monument to his enduring benevolence.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：天子待宰相以不疑，是矣。

translations.literal: The commentary says: For the Son of Heaven to treat grand councilors with undoubting trust—that is right.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: For a ruler to meet his chancellors with unwavering trust is indeed proper.

sentences.zh: 雖然，於賢不肖當別白分明，乃可與言治。

translations.literal: Nevertheless, regarding the worthy and the unworthy one ought to discriminate clearly—only then can one speak of governing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the worthy and the unworthy must be told apart with clarity before one can speak of good government.

sentences.zh: 文宗無知人之明，但以不疑責宰相。

translations.literal: Emperor Wénzōng lacked the discernment to know men and only demanded of grand councilors that they be beyond doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wénzōng had no eye for talent and merely demanded unquestioning loyalty from his chancellors.

sentences.zh: 是時善惡混淆，故黨人成於下，主聽亂於上，王室之衰，由此為之階。

translations.literal: At that time good and evil were confused; therefore factions formed below and the sovereign's hearing was disordered above—the royal house's decline had here its stairway.
translations.idiomatic: Good and evil were then hopelessly mixed, so factions rose below while the throne was misled above—the dynasty's fall began on this path.

sentences.zh: 劉向所雲「持不斷之慮者，開群枉之門」，殆文宗為邪！

translations.literal: What Liú Xiàng said—"one who holds indecisive plans opens the door to mass wrong"—probably applies to Wénzōng!
translations.idiomatic: Liú Xiàng's words, "He who cannot decide opens the gate to countless injustices," surely describe Wénzōng!

sentences.zh: 崔珙，其先博陵人。

translations.literal: Cuī Gǒng—his forebears were men of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cuī Gǒng came from a Boling family.

sentences.zh: 父颋，官同州刺史，生八子，皆有才，世以擬漢荀氏「八龍」。

translations.literal: His father Cuī Yǐng served as governor of Tongzhou and fathered eight sons, all talented; the age compared them to the Hàn Xún clan's "Eight Dragons."
translations.idiomatic: His father Cuī Yǐng was governor of Tongzhou and had eight gifted sons, whom contemporaries likened to the "Eight Dragons" of the Xún family in Hàn times.

sentences.zh: 珙為人有威重，精吏治，以拔萃異等，累擢至泗州刺史。

translations.literal: Gǒng as a man had dignity and weight, excelled in clerkly governance, and through outstanding selection in the exceptional grade was repeatedly promoted to governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gǒng was imposing in bearing and skilled in administration; chosen through the exceptional civil-service track, he rose to governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 由太府卿為嶺南節度使，入對延英，文宗訪治撫後先，珙對精亮有理趣，帝咨嗟迂久。

translations.literal: From Grand Treasury Director he became military commissioner of Lingnan; entering to answer at Yányīng, Wénzōng inquired what should come first and last in governing and soothing, and Gǒng's reply was keen, bright, and full of reason—the emperor sighed that he had been kept away so long.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted from grand treasury director to commissioner of Lingnan, he was questioned at Yányīng Hall on priorities in rule and pacification; his answers were lucid and principled, and the emperor lamented how long he had been kept from court.

sentences.zh: 時徐州以王智興後，軍驕，數犯法，節度使高瑀未能制。

translations.literal: At the time, after Wáng Zhìxīng, Xuzhou's army was arrogant and repeatedly broke the law; military commissioner Gāo Yǔ could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: After Wáng Zhìxīng's time at Xuzhou the garrison grew insolent and lawless, and Commissioner Gāo Yǔ could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 天子思材望威烈者檢革其弊，見珙意慷慨，又知治泗得士心，即謂宰相曰：「欲武寧節度使者，無易珙才。」

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sought one of talent, reputation, and stern majesty to inspect and reform these abuses; seeing Gǒng's spirit ardent and knowing that in governing Si he had won soldiers' hearts, he at once told the grand councilors: "For the Wuning military commissioner, none can replace Gǒng's ability."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted a man of ability, standing, and force to correct the abuses; finding Gǒng resolute and knowing he had won the troops' loyalty at Si, he told the chancellors: "For Wuning commissioner, no one matches Gǒng."

sentences.zh: 更詔王茂元帥嶺南，而以珙代瑀。

translations.literal: A new edict ordered Wáng Màoyuán to command Lingnan and Gǒng to replace Yǔ.
translations.idiomatic: He reassigned Wáng Màoyuán to Lingnan and sent Gǒng to replace Yǔ.

sentences.zh: 居二歲，徐人戢畏。

translations.literal: After two years the people of Xu were restrained in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years the Xuzhou soldiery were subdued and fearful.

sentences.zh: 入為右金吾大將軍，遷京兆尹。

translations.literal: He entered court as General of the Right Golden Guards and was transferred to Mayor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as general of the right golden guards and made mayor of the capital district.

sentences.zh: 會大旱，奏析浐入禁中者，取十九溉民田。

translations.literal: When a great drought occurred, he memorialized that of the Chan water diverted into the palace, nine parts in ten should irrigate the people's fields.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe drought he petitioned to divert nine-tenths of the Chan River water reserved for the palace to irrigate farmland.

sentences.zh: 仇士良使盜擊宰相李石於親仁裏，跡出禁軍，珙坐不能捕，以為負，望少衰。

translations.literal: Qiū Shìliáng sent robbers to strike Grand Councilor Lǐ Shí in Qīnrén Lane; the trail led to the forbidden army. Gǒng was blamed for failing to capture them and was thought deficient; his reputation declined somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Qiū Shìliáng had assassins attack Chancellor Lǐ Shí in Qīnrén Lane, and the trail pointed to the palace guard. Gǒng was faulted for not making arrests, and his standing suffered.

sentences.zh: 開成末，累進刑部尚書、諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaicheng era he was repeatedly advanced to Minister of Justice and Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport of all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Kaicheng he rose to minister of justice and salt-and-iron transport commissioner for all circuits.

sentences.zh: 俄同中書門下平章事，仍領鹽鐵，即拜中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly he became Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs with the Grand Councilor title, still heading salt and iron, and was at once appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand councilor while retaining the salt monopoly, and appointed vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會昌二年，進位尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huichang he was advanced to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Huichang year two he was promoted to left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，以兄琯喪，被疾求解，以所守官罷。

translations.literal: The next year, on his elder brother Guàn's mourning, he fell ill and requested release, and was dismissed from the offices he held.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, mourning his brother Guàn, he fell ill and asked to resign, and was relieved of his posts.

sentences.zh: 與崔鉉故有怨，及鉉宰相代為使，即奏珙妄費宋滑院鹽鐵錢九十萬緡，又劾與劉從諫厚，數護其奸。

translations.literal: He had an old grudge with Cuī Xuàn; when Xuàn became grand councilor and replaced him as commissioner, he at once memorialized that Gǒng had wantonly spent nine hundred thousand strings of the Song-Hua office's salt-and-iron funds, and also impeached him for closeness to Liú Cóngjiàn, repeatedly shielding his wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: He and Cuī Xuàn were old enemies; when Xuàn became chancellor and succeeded him as transport commissioner, he accused Gǒng of squandering nine hundred thousand strings from the Song-Hua salt office and of repeatedly shielding Liú Cóngjiàn's misconduct.

sentences.zh: 貶澧州刺史，再斥恩州司馬。

translations.literal: Gǒng was demoted to governor of Lǐzhou and again expelled as vice commandant of Enzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gǒng was demoted to prefect of Lǐ and then further banished as vice commandant of En.

sentences.zh: 宣宗立，徙商州刺史，以太子賓客分司東都，起為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuānzōng acceded, Gǒng was moved to governor of Shangzhou, served as Guest of the Heir Apparent with detached duty at the Eastern Capital, and was raised up as military commissioner of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuānzōng came to the throne, Gǒng was transferred to Shangzhou, served as guest of the heir on detached duty in Luoyang, then was recalled as commissioner of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 鉉復執政，珙懼，以疾自乞。

translations.literal: When Xuàn returned to power, Gǒng was afraid and pleaded illness to request release.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuàn was back in office, Gǒng, fearing him, resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 方是時，西戎歸故地，邊奏系驛，議所以綏接，珙坐不自力避事，下除太子少師，分司東都，就拜留守。

translations.literal: Just then the western Rong returned to their old lands; border reports crowded the relay stations as the court debated how to pacify and receive them. Gǒng was blamed for not exerting himself and shirking affairs; he was demoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent with detached duty at the Eastern Capital and was then appointed metropolitan guardian.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the western tribes reclaimed old territory, and frontier dispatches flooded in while the court debated how to manage them. Gǒng was faulted for evading the work; demoted to junior tutor of the heir on detached duty in Luoyang, he was soon named metropolitan guardian.

sentences.zh: 復節度鳳翔，卒於官。

translations.literal: He again commanded Fengxiang as military commissioner and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to command Fengxiang and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子涓，性開敏。

translations.literal: His son Juān was by nature open and quick.
translations.idiomatic: His son Juān was quick-witted and alert.

sentences.zh: 為杭州刺史，受署，未盡識卒史，乃以紙各署姓名傅襟上，過前一閱，後數百人呼指無誤。

translations.literal: As governor of Hangzhou, on taking his commission he had not yet fully known the clerks and runners; he therefore wrote each man's name on paper and fastened them to his collar, read them once as they passed, and afterward called out hundreds without error.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Hangzhou he had not yet learned his staff by sight; he wrote each clerk's name on a slip pinned to his robe, glanced once as they filed past, and thereafter could summon hundreds by name without mistake.

sentences.zh: 終御史大夫。

translations.literal: He ended as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 琯，字從律，珙兄。

translations.literal: Guàn, styled Cónglǜ, was Gǒng's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Guàn, courtesy name Cónglǜ, was Gǒng's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 舉進士、賢良方正，皆高第。

translations.literal: He entered the jinshi and Worthy and Upright examinations, taking high rank in both.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and the "worthy and upright" examinations with top honors.

sentences.zh: 累辟諸使府。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly recruited to various commissioners' staffs.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly invited onto commissioners' staffs.

sentences.zh: 入朝，稍歷吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered court and gradually served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he rose to vice director in the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 李德裕任御史中丞，引知雜事。

translations.literal: When Lǐ Déyù served as Vice Censor-in-Chief, he brought Guàn in to handle miscellaneous business.
translations.idiomatic: When Lǐ Déyù was vice censor-in-chief, he put Guàn in charge of routine business.

sentences.zh: 進給事中。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 太和初，持節宣慰盧龍，使有指。

translations.literal: In early Taihe he bore the staff as commissioner to proclaim comfort in Lulong; the mission had a clear aim.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe he was dispatched with imperial credentials to pacify Lulong on a mission with definite purpose.

sentences.zh: 及興元殺李絳，復往尉撫，軍皆按堵。

translations.literal: When Xingyuan killed Lǐ Jiàng, he went again to comfort and soothe; the army was entirely secure.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingyuan killed Lǐ Jiàng, he returned to calm the troops, and the garrison was restored to order.

sentences.zh: 還，遷工部侍郎、京兆尹。

translations.literal: On his return he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works and Mayor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was made vice minister of works and mayor of the capital.

sentences.zh: 宋申錫為讒所危，宦豎切齒，時罕敢辨者。

translations.literal: Sòng Shēnxī was endangered by slander; the palace eunuchs gnashed their teeth, and few at the time dared speak for him.
translations.idiomatic: Sòng Shēnxī was imperiled by calumny, and the eunuchs hated him; scarcely anyone dared defend him.

sentences.zh: 琯與大理卿王正雅固請出獄付外，與眾治之，天下重其賢。

translations.literal: Guàn and Court of Review Director Wáng Zhèngyǎ firmly requested that he be removed from prison and handed to the outer administration for trial with the public; all under Heaven esteemed their worth.
translations.idiomatic: Guàn and the chief justice Wáng Zhèngyǎ insisted he be removed from custody and tried openly; the realm honored their integrity.

sentences.zh: 以尚書右丞出為荊南節度使，進左丞。

translations.literal: As Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs he went out as military commissioner of Jingnan and was advanced to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He left court as right vice director to serve as commissioner of Jingnan, then was promoted to left vice director.

sentences.zh: 時弟珙任京兆尹，並據顯劇處，世以為榮。

translations.literal: At the time his younger brother Gǒng held the mayoralty of Jingzhao; both occupied conspicuous and strenuous posts, and the age regarded it as glory.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Gǒng was then mayor of the capital; both held weighty posts, and contemporaries took it as a family triumph.

sentences.zh: 俄判兵部西銓、吏部東銓，徙東都留守。

translations.literal: Shortly he concurrently judged the Military Bureau's western selection and the Personnel Bureau's eastern selection, then was moved to metropolitan guardian of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He soon oversaw both the western military and eastern civil selection boards, then became metropolitan guardian of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 以吏部尚書召，辭疾不拜。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Personnel but declined on grounds of illness and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as minister of personnel, he pleaded illness and refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，終山南西道節度使，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the Huichang era he ended as military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit and was posthumously given the Left Vice Directorship.
translations.idiomatic: In Huichang he finished as commissioner of Shannan West and was posthumously honored as left vice director.

sentences.zh: 琯行方介，有器蘊，人屬以為相而卒不至，當時共咨雲。

translations.literal: Guàn's conduct was square and upright, with depth of capacity; people expected him to become grand councilor, yet he never reached it—the age jointly lamented it.
translations.idiomatic: Guàn was upright and substantial, and many expected him to reach the chancellorship, but he never did—a loss widely mourned.

sentences.zh: 弟璪、玙尤顯，璪位刑部尚書，玙河中節度使。

translations.literal: Younger brothers Sǎo and Yú were especially prominent: Sǎo reached Minister of Justice, Yú military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brothers Sǎo and Yú also rose high—Sǎo to minister of justice and Yú to commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 玙子淡，舉止秀峙，時謂玉而冠者。

translations.literal: Yú's son Dàn had deportment elegant and towering; the age called him the jade that crowns all.
translations.idiomatic: Yú's son Dàn was graceful in bearing; contemporaries called him the finest jade of the age.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，累進禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was selected in the jinshi degree and was repeatedly advanced to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and rose to vice director in the ministry of rites.

sentences.zh: 當時士大夫以流品相尚，推名德者為之首。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials of the time esteemed pedigree and standing and set those of name and virtue at the head.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry of the day prized lineage and standing and ranked men of renown and virtue foremost.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，世推李都為大龍甲，涓豪放不得預，雖自抑下，猶不許，而淡與焉。

translations.literal: In the Xiantong era the age pushed Lǐ Dū as chief of the great-dragon first rank; Juān, unrestrained and bold, could not be included—even though he humbled himself, he was still not permitted, while Dàn was among them.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantong, Lǐ Dū led the elite "great dragon" circle; Juān's brash manner barred him even when he tried to defer, but Dàn was admitted.

sentences.zh: 終吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He ended as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 子遠，有文而風致整峻，世慕其為，目曰「饤座梨」，言座所珍也。

translations.literal: His son Yuǎn had literary talent and bearing stern and refined; the age admired his conduct and called him the "display-pear on the seat," meaning the treasure of the gathering.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuǎn was learned and austere in manner; admirers nicknamed him the "pear on the banquet tray," the choicest ornament of any table.

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，以兵部侍郎同中書門下平章事，遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Qianning era, as Vice Minister of War he became Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs with the Grand Councilor title and was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianning he became grand councilor from the post of vice minister of war and was promoted to vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從遷洛，罷為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Following the move to Luoyang, he was dismissed to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved to Luoyang he was removed and made right vice director.

sentences.zh: 柳璨忌衣冠有望者，貶為白州長史，被殺於白馬驛，家沒掖庭。

translations.literal: Liǔ Càn envied gentry of promise; Yuǎn was demoted to senior adjutant of Baizhou, killed at Baima Post, and his household was confiscated to the palace women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Liǔ Càn feared promising officials; Yuǎn was banished to Baizhou, murdered at Baima Post, and his family was seized for the palace workshops.

sentences.zh: 諸崔自咸通後有名，歷臺閣藩鎮者數十人，天下推士族之冠。

translations.literal: The various Cuī since Xiantong were famous; several tens served in the capital bureaus and regional commands, and all under Heaven ranked them the crown of gentry clans.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiantong the Cui produced dozens of men in central office and in the provinces, and the realm hailed them the foremost clan.

sentences.zh: 始，其曾王母長孫春秋高，無齒，祖母唐事姑孝，每旦乳姑。

translations.literal: At the beginning, his great-grandmother by marriage, née Zhǎngsūn, was advanced in years and toothless; his grandmother, née Táng, served her mother-in-law filially and each dawn nursed her.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, a great-grandmother of the line, née Zhǎngsūn, lived to great age without teeth; her daughter-in-law, née Táng, nursed her mother-in-law each morning in filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 一日病，召長幼言：「吾無以報婦，願後子孫皆若爾孝。」

translations.literal: One day, ill, she summoned young and old and said: "I have no means to repay my daughter-in-law; may later descendants all be as filial as you."
translations.idiomatic: On her deathbed she gathered the clan and said: "I cannot repay my daughter-in-law; may all our descendants show such devotion as yours."

sentences.zh: 世謂崔氏昌大有所本雲。

translations.literal: The age said the Cuī clan's flourishing greatness had its root in this.
translations.idiomatic: People said the Cui family's eminence had its source in this.

sentences.zh: 蕭鄴，字啟之，梁長沙宣王懿九世孫。

translations.literal: Xiāo Yè, styled Qǐzhī, was ninth-generation descendant of Prince Yì of Changsha of Liáng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiāo Yè, courtesy name Qǐzhī, was a ninth-generation descendant of Liáng's Prince Yì of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，累進監察御史、翰林學士，出為衡州刺史。

translations.literal: He reached the jinshi degree and was repeatedly advanced to Investigating Censor and Hanlin Academician, then went out as governor of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi graduate, he rose to investigating censor and Hanlin academician, then was posted as governor of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 大中中，召還翰林，拜中書舍人，遷戶部侍郎，判本司，以工部尚書同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong era he was recalled to the Hanlin, appointed Secretariat Drafting Official, transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue with concurrent direction of that ministry, and made Minister of Works with the Associate Director and Grand Councilor titles.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong he returned to the Hanlin, became a drafting official in the secretariat, then vice minister of revenue directing that ministry, and finally grand councilor as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 懿宗初，罷為荊南節度使，仍平章事，進檢校尚書左僕射，徙劍南西川。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yìzōng's reign he was dismissed to military commissioner of Jingnan, still a Grand Councilor, advanced to acting Left Vice Director, and moved to Jiannan West.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yìzōng's reign he was sent out as commissioner of Jingnan while retaining the councilorship, made acting left vice director, then transferred to Jiannan West.

sentences.zh: 南詔內寇，不能制，下遷檢校右僕射、山南西道觀察使。

translations.literal: Nánzhāo raided within the borders and he could not control them; he was demoted to acting Right Vice Director and observation commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Nánzhāo invaded and he failed to repel them, he was demoted to acting right vice director and observation commissioner of Shannan West.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部、吏部二尚書，拜右僕射。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of Revenue and Minister of Personnel in turn and was appointed Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He served as minister of revenue and of personnel in succession, then was appointed right vice director.

sentences.zh: 還，以平章事節度河東。

translations.literal: On his return he served as Grand Councilor while commanding Hedong as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he governed Hedong as commissioner while remaining on the council.

sentences.zh: 在官無足稱道，卒。

translations.literal: In office there was nothing worth recounting; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He accomplished little in office and died.

sentences.zh: 鄭肅，字乂敬，其先滎陽人，以儒世家。

translations.literal: Zhèng Sù, styled Yìjìng, had forebears who were men of Xingyang—a Confucian hereditary family.
translations.idiomatic: Zhèng Sù, courtesy name Yìjìng, was of a Xingyang family long devoted to classical learning.

sentences.zh: 肅力於學，有根柢。

translations.literal: Sù strove in learning and had deep roots.
translations.idiomatic: Sù studied with rigor and had a solid grounding in the classics.

sentences.zh: 第進士、書判拔萃，補興平尉。

translations.literal: He placed in the jinshi and in the outstanding selection for document judgment, and was appointed sheriff of Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and excelled in the document-judgment examination, then was appointed sheriff of Xingping.

sentences.zh: 累擢太常少卿，博士有疑議往咨，必據經條答。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; when doctors of ritual had doubtful points they went to consult him, and he always answered by canonical articles.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director of the court of imperial sacrifices; ritual specialists brought him doubtful cases, and he always answered from the canonical texts.

sentences.zh: 文宗高擇魯王府屬，肅以諫議大夫兼長史。

translations.literal: Wénzōng highly selected staff for the Prince of Lu's household, and Sù served as Remonstrance Grandee with concurrent office as chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Wénzōng carefully chose staff for the Prince of Lu, and Sù served as remonstrance official and chief administrator of the household.

sentences.zh: 王為皇太子，遷給事中，進尚書右丞。

translations.literal: When the prince became Heir Apparent, Sù was transferred to Attendant Censor and advanced to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became heir apparent, Sù was made attendant censor and then right vice director.

sentences.zh: 出為陜虢觀察使。

translations.literal: He went out as observation commissioner of Shan and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as observation commissioner of Shǎn and Guǒ.

sentences.zh: 開成二年，召拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaicheng year two he was recalled as vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝以肅嘗輔導東宮，詔兼賓客，為太子授經。

translations.literal: Because Sù had once tutored the Eastern Palace, an edict made him concurrently Guest of the Heir Apparent, lecturing the crown prince in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had once instructed the heir's household, the emperor named him also guest of the heir and had him lecture the crown prince in the classics.

sentences.zh: 既而太子母愛弛，為讒所乘，廢斥有端。

translations.literal: Before long the crown prince's mother's favor slackened; ridden by slander, his dismissal had its pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the crown prince's mother fell from favor; slander found its opening, and grounds for his removal appeared.

sentences.zh: 肅因入見，言天下大本，不可輕動，意致深切，帝為動容。

translations.literal: Sù therefore entered audience and spoke that the great foundation of the realm must not be lightly moved; his intent was deep and cutting, and the emperor was moved in countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Sù seized an audience to warn that the throne's foundation must not be lightly shaken; his plea was urgent, and the emperor was visibly moved.

sentences.zh: 然內寵方煽，太子終以憂死。

translations.literal: Yet inner favorites were then raging, and the crown prince in the end died in grief.
translations.idiomatic: But palace favorites were ascendant, and the crown prince ultimately died of grief.

sentences.zh: 出為檢校禮部尚書、河中節度使。

translations.literal: He went out as acting Minister of Rites and military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as acting minister of rites and commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 武宗知太子無罪，特困於讒，而朝廷謂肅臨義不可奪，侹侹有大臣節，召為太常卿。

translations.literal: Wǔzōng knew the crown prince was innocent and was especially grieved at the slander; the court said Sù, facing righteousness, could not be swayed—unyielding, he had the integrity of a great minister—and summoned him as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Wǔzōng knew the heir had been innocent and deeply resented the slander; the court held that Sù, faced with injustice, could not be bent—unyielding, he showed a great minister's spine—and recalled him as director of the court of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 遷山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to commissioner of Shannan East.

sentences.zh: 五年，以檢校尚書右僕射同中書門下平章事，與李德裕葉心輔政。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made acting Right Vice Director with the Associate Director and Grand Councilor titles and, of one mind with Lǐ Déyù, assisted in government.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he became acting right vice director and grand councilor and governed in concert with Lǐ Déyù.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，遷中書侍郎，罷為荊南節度使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuānzōng acceded, Sù was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and dismissed to military commissioner of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuānzōng came to the throne, Sù was made vice director of the secretariat, then sent out as commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空，謚曰文簡。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Minister of Works, with posthumous title Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as minister of works with the epithet Wenjian, "Cultivated and Simple."

sentences.zh: 子洎，仕至州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Jì served up to prefectural governor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jì rose to a prefectural governorship.

sentences.zh: 洎子仁規、仁表，皆豪爽有文。

translations.literal: Jì's sons Rén'guī and Rén'biǎo were both bold and generous and possessed literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Jì's sons Rén'guī and Rén'biǎo were both bold, open-handed, and literary.

sentences.zh: 仁規位中書舍人。

translations.literal: Rén'guī reached the office of Secretariat Drafting Official.
translations.idiomatic: Rén'guī became a drafting official in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 仁表累擢起居郎。

translations.literal: Rén'biǎo was repeatedly advanced to Attendant of the Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: Rén'biǎo rose to attendant of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 嘗以門閥文章自高，曰：「天瑞有五色雲，人瑞有鄭仁表。」

translations.literal: He once took his lineage and literary achievement as lofty and said: "Heaven's auspice has five-colored clouds; humanity's auspice has Zhèng Rén'biǎo."
translations.idiomatic: He once boasted of his pedigree and prose, saying: "Heaven's omen is the five-colored cloud; the age's omen is Zhèng Rén'biǎo."

sentences.zh: 傲縱多所陵藉，人畏薄之。

translations.literal: Proud and unrestrained, he often slighted others; people feared and despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogant and overbearing, he often insulted others, and men feared and scorned him.

sentences.zh: 劉鄴未仕，往謁洎，而仁表等鄙訿其文。

translations.literal: Before Liú Yè had taken office he went to visit Jì, but Rén'biǎo and the others despised and ridiculed his writing.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had entered office, Liú Yè called on Jì, but Rén'biǎo and his kin mocked his literary efforts.

sentences.zh: 鄴為相，因罪貶仁表，死嶺外。

translations.literal: When Yè became grand councilor, he used a charge to demote Rén'biǎo, who died beyond the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When Yè became chancellor, he found cause to banish Rén'biǎo, who died in the far south.

sentences.zh: 始，肅罷政事，帝以盧商代之。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Sù left government affairs, the emperor replaced him with Lú Shāng.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhèng Sù left the council, the emperor named Lú Shāng in his place.

sentences.zh: 商字為臣，蚤孤，家窶困，能以學自奮。

translations.literal: Shāng, styled Wéichén, was orphaned young; his household was poor and straitened, yet he could rouse himself through learning.
translations.idiomatic: Shāng, courtesy name Wéichén, lost his father early and grew up in poverty, yet drove himself forward through study.

sentences.zh: 舉進士、拔萃，皆中。

translations.literal: In the jinshi and in the tuōcuī examination he hit the mark in both.
translations.idiomatic: He passed both the jinshi examination and the advanced selection.

sentences.zh: 由校書郎佐宣歙、西川幕府。

translations.literal: From Collator he served on the staff of Xuān- and Shè-circuits and of Xīchuān.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a collator, he served on the staffs of the Xuān and Shè region and of Xīchuān.

sentences.zh: 入朝，累十餘遷，至大理卿。

translations.literal: Entering court, through more than ten promotions he reached Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Called to the capital, he rose through more than ten postings to director of the court of judicial review.

sentences.zh: 為蘇州刺史，吏以鹽法求贏貲，民愈困，商令計口售鹽，無常額，人便之，歲貲返增。

translations.literal: As governor of Sūzhōu, clerks used the salt law to seek surplus levies and the people grew yet more distressed; Shāng ordered salt sold by head count without a fixed quota; people found it convenient, and the annual tribute shipment actually increased.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Sūzhōu, where officials had squeezed extra profit from the salt monopoly and deepened the people's hardship, he ordered salt sold per capita at no fixed quota—a measure the people welcomed—and annual remittances to the court actually rose.

sentences.zh: 宰相上其勞，進浙西觀察使，召為刑部侍郎、京兆尹。

translations.literal: The grand councilors memorialized his merit; he was advanced to observation commissioner of Zhèxī and summoned as Vice Minister of Justice and Intendant of Jīngzhào.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors cited his achievements; he was promoted to commissioner of Zhèxī, then recalled as vice minister of justice and intendant of the capital district.

sentences.zh: 方伐潞，芻糧逾太行餉軍，環六七鎮，詔商以戶部侍郎判度支，又詔杜悰兼鹽鐵、度支，並二使財以贍兵，乃不乏。

translations.literal: Just then they were attacking Lù; fodder and grain were sent over the Tàiháng Mountains to supply the army, circling six or seven prefectures; an edict ordered Shāng, as Vice Minister of Revenue, to oversee the Bureau of Revenue; another edict made Dù Zōng concurrently oversee Salt and Iron and Revenue; they combined the two bureaus' funds to provision the troops, and supplies did not fail.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Lù, fodder crossed the Tàiháng to feed armies across six or seven circuits. Shāng was ordered to run the revenue bureau as vice minister of revenue; Dù Zōng was also named to the salt and iron and revenue posts. By pooling both agencies' funds they kept the armies supplied.

sentences.zh: 出為東川節度使，以兵部侍郎還判度支，擢中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，范陽郡公。

translations.literal: He went out as military commissioner of East Chuān; returning as Vice Minister of War he again oversaw the Bureau of Revenue; he was elevated to Vice Director of the Secretariat, Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Councilor, and ennobled Duke of Fànyáng.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as commissioner of East Chuān, he returned as vice minister of war to run the revenue bureau again, then rose to vice director of the secretariat, grand councilor, and Duke of Fànyáng.

sentences.zh: 大中元年春旱，詔商與御史中丞封敖理囚系於尚書省，誤縱死罪，罷為武昌軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the spring drought of the first year of Dàzhōng, an edict ordered Shāng and Vice Censor-in-Chief Fēng Áo to handle prisoners in the Ministry of Justice; they mistakenly released men under death sentence and were dismissed—Shāng to military commissioner of the Wǔchāng army.
translations.idiomatic: In a drought year of Dàzhōng's first year, Shāng and vice censor-in-chief Fēng Áo were ordered to review prisoners at the Ministry of Justice. They mistakenly freed men under death sentence. Shāng was demoted to commissioner of Wǔchāng.

sentences.zh: 以疾解，拜戶部尚書，卒。

translations.literal: On illness he was released from office; he was appointed Minister of Revenue and died.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness, was named minister of revenue, and died.

sentences.zh: 盧鈞，字子和，系出范陽，徙京兆藍田。

translations.literal: Lú Jūn, styled Zǐhé, traced his line to Fànyáng and moved to Lántian in Jīngzhào.
translations.idiomatic: Lú Jūn, courtesy name Zǐhé, came of a Fànyáng clan that had settled in Lántian in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 舉進士中第，以拔萃補秘書正字。

translations.literal: He placed in the jinshi and, through tuōcuī, was appointed Proofreader in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and, on the advanced selection, became a proofreader in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從李絳為山南府推官，調長安尉。

translations.literal: Following Lǐ Jiàng he was a judicial aide in the Shānnán office; he was transferred to sheriff of Cháng'ān.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Lǐ Jiàng as a judicial aide in Shānnán, then was posted as sheriff of Cháng'ān.

sentences.zh: 又從裴度為太原觀察支使，遷監察御史，爭宋申錫獄知名。

translations.literal: Again following Péi Dù he was supporting commissioner of the Tàiyuán observation office; he was promoted to Supervising Censor and became famous for disputing the case of Sòng Shēnxī.
translations.idiomatic: Under Péi Dù he served as staff commissioner at Tàiyuán, then became supervising censor and won renown for his stand in the Sòng Shēnxī affair.

sentences.zh: 進吏部郎中，出為常州刺史。

translations.literal: He advanced to Langzhong in the Ministry of Personnel and went out as prefect of Chángzhōu.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to a director in the Ministry of Personnel, he went out as governor of Chángzhōu.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中，有大詔令，必反覆省審，駁奏無私。

translations.literal: Transferred to Attendant Censor, whenever there was a great edict he invariably reviewed it back and forth; his refuting memorials were without private motive.
translations.idiomatic: As attendant censor, he scrutinized every major edict repeatedly and filed refusals without favoritism.

sentences.zh: 拜華州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of Huázhōu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Huázhōu.

sentences.zh: 關輔驛馬疲耗，鈞為市健馬，率三歲一易，自是無乏事。

translations.literal: In the Guānfu region relay horses were worn out and depleted; Jūn bought strong horses, on average replacing them every three years, and from then on there were no shortages in service.
translations.idiomatic: Relay horses in the capital approaches were exhausted; Jūn purchased strong replacements on a three-year cycle, and shortages ceased.

sentences.zh: 擢嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: He was elevated to military commissioner of Língnán.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commissioner of Língnán.

sentences.zh: 海道商舶始至，異時帥府爭先往，賤售其珍，鈞一不取，時稱絜廉。

translations.literal: When merchant ships first arrived by sea route, at other times the commander's office all raced to go first and sold their treasures cheap; Jūn took not one thing, and the times called him pure and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: When the first sea-traders arrived, commanders had habitually rushed to buy their goods cheap; Jūn took nothing, and men praised his scrupulous probity.

sentences.zh: 專以清靜治。

translations.literal: He governed solely by quietness and purity.
translations.idiomatic: He governed through quiet restraint.

sentences.zh: 蕃獠與華人錯居，相婚嫁，多占田營第舍，吏或撓之，則相為亂；

translations.literal: Tribal peoples of Fán and Liáo lived mingled with Chinese, intermarrying; they largely seized fields and built residences; if clerks sometimes impeded them they would mutually incite disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Tribal peoples and Han Chinese lived intermingled and intermarried, often seizing land and building mansions; when officials interfered, the communities rioted;

sentences.zh: 鈞下令蕃華不得通婚，禁名田產，闔部肅壹無敢犯。

translations.literal: Jūn issued orders that Fán and Chinese might not intermarry and forbade nominal ownership of fields; the whole territory was solemnly unified and none dared violate.
translations.idiomatic: Jūn forbade intermarriage between tribes and Han Chinese and banned illegal landholding; the whole territory fell in line and none dared defy him.

sentences.zh: 貞元後流放衣冠，其子姓窮弱不能自還者，為營棺槥還葬，有疾若喪則經給醫藥、殯斂，孤女稚兒，為立夫家，以奉稟資助，凡數百家。

translations.literal: After Zhēnyuán, exiled courtiers—those whose sons and surnames were poor and weak and could not return on their own—he arranged coffins to return them for burial; when there was illness or mourning he provided medicine and funeral goods; for orphaned girls and young boys he established households for them and supported them with stipend aid—in all several hundred families.
translations.idiomatic: For families of officials banished after the Zhēnyuán era who could not afford the journey home, he provided coffins and burial transport; he supplied medicine and funeral costs for the sick and bereaved; he found husbands for orphaned girls and support for young sons—aiding several hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 南方服其德，不懲而化。

translations.literal: The south submitted to his virtue; without punishment they were transformed.
translations.idiomatic: The south submitted to his virtue and was reformed without coercion.

sentences.zh: 又除采金稅。

translations.literal: He also abolished the gold-mining tax.
translations.idiomatic: He also abolished the gold-mining tax.

sentences.zh: 華、蠻數千走闕下，請為鈞生立祠，刻石頌德，鈞固辭。

translations.literal: Several thousand Chinese and tribal people ran to the palace gates, asking to establish a living shrine for Jūn and carve stone praising his virtue; Jūn firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of Han and tribal subjects went to the capital to ask leave for a living shrine and commemorative stele; Jūn firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 以戶部侍郎召判戶部。

translations.literal: Summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue, he concurrently oversaw the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as vice minister of revenue, he concurrently ran the ministry.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，漢水害襄陽，拜鈞山南東道節度使，築堤六千步，以障漢暴。

translations.literal: In Huìchāng, the Hàn River harmed Xiāngyáng; Jūn was appointed military commissioner of Shānnán East Circuit and built a dike six thousand paces long to block the Hàn's violence.
translations.idiomatic: During Huìchāng, when the Hàn River devastated Xiāngyáng, Jūn was named commissioner of Shānnán East and built a six-thousand-pace levee against the floods.

sentences.zh: 王師伐劉稹，武宗以鈞寬厚能得眾，詔兼節度昭義軍。

translations.literal: Imperial forces attacked Liú Zhěn; Wǔzōng, considering Jūn generous and able to win the masses, ordered him also to be military commissioner of the Zhàoyì army.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial armies marched against Liú Zhěn, Wǔzōng—trusting Jūn's open hand with troops—named him also commissioner of the Zhàoyì army.

sentences.zh: 會稹死，敕乘驲往，進檢校兵部尚書，專領昭義。

translations.literal: When Zhěn died, an edict ordered him to go by relay horse; he was advanced to acting Minister of War and solely held Zhàoyì.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhěn died, he was ordered to ride post-horses to the front, promoted to acting minister of war, and given sole charge of Zhàoyì.

sentences.zh: 鈞及潞，石雄兵已入，而稹將白惟信率餘卒三千保潞，城未下。

translations.literal: When Jūn reached Lù, Shí Xióng's troops had already entered, yet Zhěn's general Bái Wéixìn led three thousand remaining soldiers to hold Lù; the city was not yet taken.
translations.idiomatic: Jūn reached Lù after Shí Xióng's troops had entered, but Zhěn's general Bái Wéixìn still held the city with three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 雄召之，使往十餘輩皆死。

translations.literal: Xióng summoned him; more than ten envoys sent went and all died.
translations.idiomatic: Xióng sent envoys to summon him; more than a dozen went and all were killed.

sentences.zh: 鈞次高平，惟信獻款，且曰：「不即降者，畏石尚書爾。」

translations.literal: Jūn halted at Gāopíng; Wéixìn offered allegiance and said: "Those who do not promptly submit fear Minister Shí alone."
translations.idiomatic: At Gāopíng, Wéixìn submitted and said, "We hesitate to surrender only because we fear Minister Shí."

sentences.zh: 鈞與約而遣。

translations.literal: Jūn made terms with him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Jūn agreed to terms and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 方雄欲盡夷潞兵，鈞不聽，坐治堂上，左右皆雄親卒，擊鼓傳漏，鈞自居甚安，雄引去，乃召惟信至，送闕下，餘眾悉原。

translations.literal: Just then Xióng wished utterly to exterminate the Lù soldiers; Jūn did not listen. He sat and conducted governance in the hall; left and right were all Xióng's intimate soldiers; drums were beaten and the clepsydra passed—Jūn himself was very composed. Xióng withdrew; then Jūn summoned Wéixìn to come, sent him to the palace gates, and pardoned all the rest of the masses.
translations.idiomatic: As Xióng was poised to slaughter the garrison, Jūn refused. He held court surrounded by Xióng's own troops while drums beat and the water-clock marked the hours, himself perfectly calm. When Xióng left, he summoned Wéixìn, sent him to the capital, and pardoned the rest.

sentences.zh: 俄而興士五千戍代北，鈞坐城門勞遣，帷家人以觀。

translations.literal: Before long five thousand fresh soldiers were garrisoned on the northern frontier; Jūn sat at the city gate to see them off with consolation, curtaining his family to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Soon five thousand fresh recruits were sent north; Jūn saw them off at the gate, with his family watching from behind a screen.

sentences.zh: 戍卒驕，顧家屬不欲去，酒酣，反攻城，迫大將李文矩為帥，鈞倉卒奔潞城。

translations.literal: The garrison soldiers were arrogant; looking at their families they did not wish to go; when wine was deep they turned and assaulted the city, forcing the great general Lǐ Wénjǔ to be commander; Jūn in haste fled to Lù city.
translations.idiomatic: The troops, drunk and reluctant to leave their families, mutinied, besieged the city, and forced General Lǐ Wénjǔ to lead them; Jūn fled in haste to the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 文矩投地僵臥，稍諭叛者，眾乃悔服，即相與謝鈞，迎還府，斬首惡乃定。

translations.literal: Wénjǔ threw himself to the ground and lay stiff; gradually he persuaded the rebels; the masses then repented and submitted; they together apologized to Jūn and welcomed him back to the headquarters; they beheaded the chief wrongdoers and it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Wénjǔ threw himself down as if dead until he had talked the mutineers around; repentant, they apologized to Jūn, escorted him back, and beheaded the ringleaders to restore order.

sentences.zh: 詔趣戍者行，密使盡戮之。

translations.literal: An edict urged the garrison soldiers to march; secret envoys were to slaughter them all.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the troops to march north and secretly authorized their wholesale execution.

sentences.zh: 鈞請徐乘其變，而使者不發，須報。

translations.literal: Jūn requested to wait and exploit their change slowly, but the envoy did not depart—he had to await report.
translations.idiomatic: Jūn asked leave to act when the moment ripened, but the imperial messenger would not move without fresh orders.

sentences.zh: 時戍人已去潞一舍，鈞選牙卒五百，壯騎百，以騎載兵夜趨；

translations.literal: At that time the garrison men had already left Lù by one station; Jūn selected five hundred guardsmen and a hundred stalwart riders, carrying the infantry by horse in night haste;
translations.idiomatic: By then the mutineers were one post-stage from Lù; Jūn picked five hundred guards and a hundred picked horsemen, and by night carried infantry on horseback in pursuit;

sentences.zh: 遲明，至太平驛，盡斬之。

translations.literal: Near dawn he reached Tàipíng Post and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he reached Tàipíng Post and cut them all down.

sentences.zh: 即拜檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was at once made acting left vice director.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，改吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuānzōng acceded he was changed to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuānzōng came to the throne, Jūn became minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 會劉約自天平徙宣武，未至，暴死。

translations.literal: When Liú Yuē was transferred from Tiānpíng to Xuānwǔ, before he arrived he died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Liú Yuē was transferring from Tiānpíng to Xuānwǔ when he died suddenly en route.

sentences.zh: 家僮五百無所仰衣食，思亂，乃授鈞宣武節度使，人情妥然。
