translations.literal: Five hundred household slaves had no one to rely on for food and clothing and thought of rebellion; the post was then given to Jūn as military commissioner of Xuānwǔ, and popular feeling was settled.
translations.idiomatic: His five hundred retainers faced ruin and mutiny loomed; appointing Jūn commissioner of Xuānwǔ settled every heart.

sentences.zh: 召入，復為吏部尚書，遷檢校司空、太子少師，封范陽郡公，節度河東。

translations.literal: Summoned in, he again became Minister of Personnel; he was transferred to acting Minister of Works, Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, ennobled Duke of Fànyáng Commandery, and made military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he again headed personnel, then rose to acting minister of works, junior mentor to the heir, Duke of Fànyáng, and commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 大中九年，召為左僕射。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dàzhōng he was summoned as Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In Dàzhōng year nine he was recalled as left vice director.

sentences.zh: 鈞宿齒，數外遷，而後來多至宰相。

translations.literal: Jūn was of long standing in years; he had been transferred outward several times, while those who came later mostly reached grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Elder in years and repeatedly posted to the provinces while younger men rose to the chancellorship,

sentences.zh: 始被召，自以當輔政，既失誌，故內怨望，數移病不事事，邀遊林墅，累日一還。

translations.literal: When first summoned he thought he ought to assist in government; having lost that aim, he therefore harbored inner resentment, repeatedly pleading illness and not handling affairs, inviting himself to roam forest estates for days before returning once.
translations.idiomatic: he had expected this recall to mean the council; disappointed, he nursed a private grievance, pleaded illness to shirk duty, and wandered his estates for days on end.

sentences.zh: 令狐惡之，罷僕射，以檢校司空守太子太師。

translations.literal: Líng Hú hated him, removed him from vice director, and had him as acting Minister of Works hold the post of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Líng Hú turned on him, stripped him of the vice directorship, and kept him only as acting minister of works and grand mentor to the heir.

sentences.zh: 帝元日大饗含元殿，鈞年八十，升降如儀，音吐鴻暢，舉朝咨嘆。

translations.literal: On the emperor's New Year great feast in Hányuán Hall, Jūn was eighty years old; ascending and descending like ritual, his voice full and flowing—the whole court sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: At the New Year feast in Hányuán Hall, eighty-year-old Jūn mounted and descended the steps with perfect grace, his voice ringing clear—the whole court marveled.

sentences.zh: 以鈞耆碩長者，顧不任職，咎為冒賢。

translations.literal: Because Jūn was a venerable elder, yet he would not bear office, blame fell that he usurped the place of the talented.
translations.idiomatic: Because such a revered elder held a title yet served no function, critics charged that he was blocking worthier men.

sentences.zh: 聞，言於帝，即以鈞同中書門下平章事，為山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: When this was heard, he spoke to the emperor, and Jūn was at once made Associate Director and Grand Councilor and military commissioner of Shānnán West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he named Jūn grand councilor and sent him out as commissioner of Shānnán West.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校司徒，為東都留守。

translations.literal: Before long he was acting Minister of Education and remained at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made acting minister of education and guardian of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 懿宗初，復節度宣武，辭不拜，以太保致仕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yìzōng's reign he was again made military commissioner of Xuānwǔ; he declined and did not accept, retiring as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: At Yìzōng's accession he was again offered Xuānwǔ but declined and retired as grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十七，贈太傅，謚曰元。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-seven; posthumously he was made Grand Tutor, with posthumous title Yuán.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-seven, was posthumously honored as grand tutor, and given the epithet Yuán.

sentences.zh: 鈞與人交，始若淡薄，既久乃益固。

translations.literal: Jūn in befriending others at first seemed thin and cold; after long time it grew ever firmer.
translations.idiomatic: In friendship he seemed aloof at first, yet bonds deepened with time.

sentences.zh: 所居官必有績，大抵根仁恕至誠而施於事。

translations.literal: In every office he occupied there was achievement—generally rooted in benevolence, forbearance, and utmost sincerity applied to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Every post he held showed results, rooted in sincere humanity and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 玩服不為鮮明，位將相，沒而無贏財。

translations.literal: Playthings and garments were not made dazzling bright; though he reached minister and councilor, when he died there was no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He wore no finery even as a minister; when he died he left no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 盧簡方，失其系世，不知所以進。

translations.literal: Lú Jiǎnfāng lost his lineage record; it is not known how he advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Lú Jiǎnfāng's pedigree was not recorded; how he entered office is unknown.

sentences.zh: 盧鈞鎮太原，表為節度府判官。

translations.literal: When Lú Jūn governed Tàiyuán he memorialized him as administrative aide of the commissioner's office.
translations.idiomatic: When Jūn held Tàiyuán, he recommended Jiǎnfāng as chief aide on his staff.

sentences.zh: 會党項羌叛，鈞使簡方督兵乘邊，旁河相險，集樹堡鄣，自神山至鹿泉縣，三百里，扈遏其沖，賊不得騁，候邏便之。

translations.literal: When the Dǎngxiàng Qiang rebelled, Jūn sent Jiǎnfāng to supervise troops along the border; beside the river they took vantage points and gathered timber for fortresses and stockades from Shénshān to Lùquán county—three hundred lǐ—guarding and blocking their thrust; the bandits could not run free; patrol and scouting were convenient.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dǎngxiàng rebellion, Jūn put Jiǎnfāng in charge of frontier troops, building fortifications along three hundred lǐ of the river from Shénshān to Lùquán to choke raiders' routes and ease border patrols.

sentences.zh: 累遷江州刺史。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he became prefect of Jiāngzhōu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to governor of Jiāngzhōu.

sentences.zh: 徙大同軍防禦使，大開屯田，練兵侈鬥，沙陀畏附。

translations.literal: Transferred to defender of the Dàtóng army, he greatly opened military colonies and drilled troops to magnify combat; the Shātóu feared and attached themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Posted to defend the Dàtóng army, he expanded military colonies, drilled fierce fighters, and won the Shātóu's fearful loyalty.

sentences.zh: 擢義昌節度使，入拜太仆卿，領大同節度。

translations.literal: Elevated to military commissioner of Yìchāng, he entered court as Grand Master of the Stud and headed Dàtóng commission.
translations.idiomatic: Made commissioner of Yìchāng, he entered court as grand master of the stud and retained command of Dàtóng.

sentences.zh: 久之，徙振武軍，道病卒。

translations.literal: After long time he was transferred to the Zhènwǔ army; on the road he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Later transferred to Zhènwǔ, he died of illness en route.

sentences.zh: 韋琮，字禮玉，世顯仕。

translations.literal: Wéi Cóng, styled Lǐyù, for generations served prominently.
translations.idiomatic: Wéi Cóng, courtesy name Lǐyù, came from a long line of eminent officials.

sentences.zh: 琮進士及第，稍進殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Cóng passed the jinshi and gradually advanced to Attendant Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Cóng passed the jinshi and rose to attendant imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 坐訊獄不得實，改太常博士。

translations.literal: Having sat in examination of a legal case without getting the facts, he was changed to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After mishandling a criminal inquiry, he was demoted to ritual scholar in the court of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 擢累戶部侍郎、翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: Elevated and repeatedly [reached] Vice Minister of Revenue and Chief Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of revenue and chief Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 以中書侍郎同中書門下平章事，遷門下侍郎兼禮部尚書，無功。

translations.literal: As Vice Director of the Secretariat, Associate Director and Grand Councilor; transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery with concurrent Minister of Rites—without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice director of the secretariat and grand councilor, then as vice director of the chancellery and minister of rites, but accomplished nothing.

sentences.zh: 罷為太子賓客分司，卒。

translations.literal: Dismissed to Guest of the Heir Apparent in the separate office; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Removed to honorary mentor of the heir in the eastern office, he died.

sentences.zh: 周墀，字德升，本汝南人。

translations.literal: Zhōu Chí, styled Déshēng, was originally a man of Rǔnán.
translations.idiomatic: Zhōu Chí, courtesy name Déshēng, was originally from Rǔnán.

sentences.zh: 少孤，事母孝。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he served his mother with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was devoted to his mother.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，辟湖南團練府巡官，入為監察御史、集賢殿學士。

translations.literal: When he reached the jinshi degree he was recruited as patrol officer of the Húnán training commission; he entered as Supervising Censor and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: After his jinshi degree he joined the Húnán defense staff, then entered court as supervising censor and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 長史學，屬辭高古，文宗雅重之。

translations.literal: He excelled in the study of history; his compositions were lofty and ancient; Wénzōng elegantly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: A skilled historian who wrote in a lofty archaic style, he won Wénzōng's special regard.

sentences.zh: 李宗閔鎮山南，表行軍司馬，閱歲召還。

translations.literal: When Lǐ Zōngmǐn governed Shānnán he memorialized him as campaigning army marshal; after a year he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: When Lǐ Zōngmǐn held Shānnán, Chí served as his army marshal and was recalled after a year.

sentences.zh: 太和末，訓、註亂政，以黨語汙搢紳有名士，分逐之，獨墀雖嘗為宗閔所禮，不能以罪誣也。

translations.literal: At the end of Tàihé, Xùn and Zhù threw government into disorder; with faction language they defiled eminent scholars and gentry of name and drove them away separately; Chí alone, though once treated with courtesy by Zōngmǐn, could not be charged with crime.
translations.idiomatic: In late Tàihé, when Zhù and Xùn's faction purged famous scholars with smears, Chí alone—though once favored by Zōngmǐn—escaped false accusation.

sentences.zh: 遷起居舍人，改考功員外郎，兼舍人事。

translations.literal: Transferred to Attendant of the Imperial Diary; changed to Outer Department Member in the Bureau of Appointments with concurrent diary duties.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to diarist, then made an outer director in the appointments bureau while keeping diary duties.

sentences.zh: 帝禦紫宸，與宰相語事已，或召左右史咨質所宜，墀最為天子欽矚。

translations.literal: When the emperor attended Zǐchén and, after discussing affairs with grand councilors, sometimes summoned the Left and Right Historians to consult on what was fitting, Chí was most looked upon with imperial esteem.
translations.idiomatic: After audience at Zǐchén Hall the emperor sometimes consulted the court historians on propriety—Chí won the deepest imperial trust.

sentences.zh: 俄知制誥，入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: Before long he was made drafting edicts; he entered the Hanlin as academician.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he drafted edicts and entered the Hanlin as academician.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，以疾改工部侍郎，出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: When Wǔzōng acceded, on illness he was changed to Vice Minister of Works and went out as governor of Huázhōu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wǔzōng came to the throne, citing illness Chí became vice minister of works and then governor of Huázhōu.

sentences.zh: 徙江西觀察使。

translations.literal: Transferred to observation commissioner of Jiāngxī.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as commissioner of Jiāngxī.

sentences.zh: 劾舉部刺史，翦捕劇賊，出兵戍彭蠡湖，禁止剽劫。

translations.literal: He impeached and recommended provincial governors, cut down and captured violent bandits, sent troops to garrison Pénglí Lake, and forbade plunder and robbery.
translations.idiomatic: He disciplined negligent governors, crushed major bandit gangs, garrisoned Pénglí Lake, and suppressed river piracy.

sentences.zh: 進拜義成節度使，封汝南縣男。

translations.literal: Advanced and appointed military commissioner of Yìchéng; ennobled Baron of Rǔnán county.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to commissioner of Yìchéng and ennobled as Baron of Rǔnán.

sentences.zh: 宿將暴謷不循令者，墀命鞭其背，一軍大治。

translations.literal: Veteran generals who were violent and insolent and did not follow orders—Chí ordered their backs flogged; the whole army was greatly governed.
translations.idiomatic: He had insubordinate senior officers flogged on the back, and the army came to rigid order.

sentences.zh: 以兵部侍郎召判度支，進同中書門下平章事、遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Summoned as Vice Minister of War to oversee the Bureau of Revenue; advanced to Associate Director and Grand Councilor and transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as vice minister of war to run the revenue bureau, he rose to grand councilor and vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 建言：「故宰相德裕重定《元和實錄》，竄寄它事，以廣父功。

translations.literal: He offered a memorial: "The former grand councilor Déyù revised the Veritable Records of the Yuánhé era, inserting extraneous matters to enlarge his father's merit.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Former Chancellor Déyù's revision of the Veritable Records of the Yuánhé era inserted extraneous material to magnify his father's deeds.

sentences.zh: 凡人君尚不改史，取必信也。」

translations.literal: For every ruler it is esteemed not to alter history, so that what is taken will be trustworthy."
translations.idiomatic: A ruler must not tamper with history if the record is to be trusted."

sentences.zh: 遂削新書。

translations.literal: The new book was thereupon cut.
translations.idiomatic: The revised portions were struck from the record.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使王宰重賂權幸，求同平章事，領宣武，墀言：「天下大鎮如並、汴者才幾，宰之求何可厭？」

translations.literal: Hedong military commissioner Wáng Zǎi heavily bribed the powerful and favored, seeking the Associate Director title and to head Xuānwǔ. Chí said: "Great prefectures under Heaven like Bìng and Biàn are only a few—how can Zǎi's demands not be sated?"
translations.idiomatic: Hedong commissioner Wáng Zǎi, bribing palace favorites, sought the chancellorship and command of Xuānwǔ too. Chí objected: "How many circuits rank with Tàiyuán or Biànliáng—and how much more does Wáng Zǎi intend to take?"

sentences.zh: 宣宗納之。

translations.literal: Xuānzōng adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuānzōng agreed.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉韋讓求為京兆，持不與。

translations.literal: Empress's consort Wéi Ràng sought to be Jīngzhào Intendant; Chí firmly did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess's husband Wéi Ràng sought the capital intendant's post, Chí flatly refused.

sentences.zh: 繇是妄進者少衰。

translations.literal: From this, reckless advancement somewhat declined.
translations.idiomatic: Unworthy promotions thereafter slackened.

sentences.zh: 會吐蕃微弱，以三州七關自歸。

translations.literal: When Tǔbō was weak and submitted on its own the three prefectures and seven passes.
translations.idiomatic: When weakening Tibet offered the return of three prefectures and seven passes,

sentences.zh: 帝召宰相議河湟事，墀對不合旨，罷為劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: the emperor summoned grand councilors to discuss Héhuáng affairs; Chí's reply did not accord with the imperial intent, and he was dismissed to military commissioner of Eastern Chuān in Jiànnán.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor convened the council on the northwest; Chí's advice missed the mark, and he was sent out as commissioner of Eastern Chuān.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉鄭顥言於帝曰：「世謂墀以直言相，亦以直言免。」

translations.literal: Empress's consort Zhèng Hào said to the emperor: "The world says Chí became councilor for blunt speech, and was removed for blunt speech as well."
translations.idiomatic: The princess's husband Zhèng Hào told the emperor, "Men say Chí entered the council for frank counsel and left it for the same."

sentences.zh: 帝悟，加拜檢校尚書右僕射，卒，年五十九，贈司徒。

translations.literal: The emperor took the point, and additionally appointed Chí Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; he died at age fifty-nine, and was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw the point and promoted Chí to acting right vice director of the Department of State Affairs. He died at fifty-nine and was posthumously ennobled as grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 裴休，字公美，孟州濟源人。

translations.literal: Pei Xiū, styled Gōngměi, was a man of Jìyuán in Mèngzhōu.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xiū, courtesy name Gōngměi, came from Jìyuán in Mèngzhōu.

sentences.zh: 父肅，貞元時為浙東觀察使，劇賊栗锽誘山越為亂，陷州縣，肅引州兵破禽之，自記平賊一篇上之，德宗嘉美。

translations.literal: His father Sù, in the Zhēnyuán era was Eastern Zhèjiāng observation commissioner; the violent bandit Lì Chéng incited the Shānyuè to rebel, seized prefectures and counties; Sù led prefectural troops, broke them, and captured him; he himself wrote a piece on pacifying the bandits and submitted it; Dézōng praised it.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sù served as commissioner of Eastern Zhèjiāng under Zhēnyuán. When the outlaw Lì Chéng stirred the Shānyuè to revolt and overran local districts, Sù led prefectural troops, defeated him, and took him alive. He then memorialized with his own account of the campaign, which Dézōng commended.

sentences.zh: 生三子。

translations.literal: He fathered three sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons.

sentences.zh: 休，仲子也，操守嚴正。

translations.literal: Xiū was the second son; his conduct and integrity were stern and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Xiū was the middle son, known for stern integrity.

sentences.zh: 方兒童時，兄弟偕隱家墅，晝講經，夜著書，終年不出戶。

translations.literal: While still a child, the brothers together retired to the family estate; by day they lectured on the classics, by night they composed books, and for a whole year did not go out the door.
translations.idiomatic: As boys the brothers withdrew to the family estate, studying the classics by day and writing at night, and did not leave the house for a full year.

sentences.zh: 有饋鹿者，諸生共薦之，休不食，曰：「疏食猶不足，今一啖肉，後何以繼？」

translations.literal: When someone presented a deer, the students together recommended it; Xiū would not eat, saying: "With plain food we still have not enough—if I take one bite of meat now, how shall I keep it up afterward?"
translations.idiomatic: When a deer was sent as a gift and his fellow students urged him to share it, Xiū refused: "Plain fare is scarce enough; one bite of meat today—how would I justify more tomorrow?"

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，舉賢良方正異等。

translations.literal: He was selected in the jinshi degree; he was recommended in the Exalted and Good and Upright category with exceptional grade.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was nominated in the exalted and upright category at the highest grade.

sentences.zh: 歷諸府辟署，入為監察御史，更內外任。

translations.literal: He passed through appointments to various prefectural staff offices, entered as investigating censor, and alternated inner and outer posts.
translations.idiomatic: After serving on several prefectural staffs he became an investigating censor and moved between capital and provincial posts.

sentences.zh: 至大中時，以兵部侍郎領諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: By the Dàzhōng era he was Vice Minister of War and concurrently commissioner of salt, iron, and transport for all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dàzhōng period he was vice minister of war and head of the salt, iron, and transport service.

sentences.zh: 六年，進同中書門下平章事，即奏言：「宰相論政上前，知印者次為時政記，所論非一，詳己辭，略它議，事有所缺，史氏莫得詳。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was advanced to Associate Director and Grand Councilor, and at once memorialized: "When grand councilors discuss policy before the throne, the seal-holder next drafts the Current Policy Record; what is discussed is not one matter—they detail their own words and abbreviate others' deliberations; where matters are lacking, the historians cannot obtain detail.
translations.idiomatic: In his sixth year in office he became grand councilor and at once proposed: "When councilors debate before the throne, the seal-holder drafts the policy record. Because each man details only his own remarks and skimps on colleagues' points, the historians never get the full picture.

sentences.zh: 請宰相人自為記，合付史官。」

translations.literal: I ask that each councilor keep his own record, to be delivered together to the historiographers."
translations.idiomatic: Let each councilor keep his own record and submit the set to the historiography office.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 進中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太和後，歲漕江、淮米四十萬斛，至渭河倉者才十三，舟楫僨敗，吏乘為奸，冒沒百端，劉晏之法盡廢。

translations.literal: After Tàihé, each year forty myriad hu of Jiāng and Huái rice were transported by canal; only about thirteen myriad reached the Wèi River granaries; boats were wrecked; officials seized the chance for villainy; embezzlement took every form; Liú Yàn's methods were wholly abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: After Tàihé, four hundred thousand hu of grain were shipped annually from the Jiāng and Huái region, yet only about a third reached the Wèi granaries. Wrecks multiplied, officials turned the system to fraud, and Liú Yàn's reforms were dead letter.

sentences.zh: 休分遣官詢按其弊，乃命在所令長兼董漕，褒能者，謫怠者。

translations.literal: Xiū sent officials separately to inquire and investigate the abuses; then he ordered the local magistrates to oversee transport concurrently; he rewarded the capable and demoted the slack.
translations.idiomatic: Xiū dispatched investigators to trace the abuses, then made local magistrates responsible for transport, rewarding diligence and punishing neglect.

sentences.zh: 由江抵渭，舊歲率雇緡二十八萬，休悉歸諸吏，敕巡院不得輒侵牟。

translations.literal: From the river to the Wèi, formerly each year on average two hundred eighty thousand strings in hire money were spent; Xiū returned it all to the transport clerks and ordered the patrol offices not to encroach or extort at will.
translations.idiomatic: The old annual hiring costs from the Yangtze to the Wèi ran to 280,000 strings of cash; Xiū turned the funds back to the transport clerks and forbade patrol offices from extorting merchants.

sentences.zh: 著新法十條，又立稅茶十二法，人以為便。

translations.literal: He composed ten articles of new law, and also established twelve articles on the tea tax; people regarded them as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted ten new regulations and twelve articles on the tea tax, which the public found workable.

sentences.zh: 居三年，粟至渭倉者百二十萬斛，無留壅。

translations.literal: After three years, grain reaching the Wèi granaries was one million two hundred myriad hu, with no backlog or obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years deliveries to the Wèi granaries rose to 1.2 million hu with no backlog.

sentences.zh: 時方鎮設邸閣居茶取直，因視商人它貨橫賦之，道路苛擾。

translations.literal: At the time military governors set up lodge offices to store tea and take commission; they then levied merchants' other goods at will; the roads were harshly troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Military governors had set up lodge offices to warehouse tea and collect fees, then imposed arbitrary levies on merchants' other goods, harassing the highways.

sentences.zh: 休建言：「許收邸直，毋擅賦商人。」

translations.literal: Xiū offered a memorial: "Permit collection of lodge commission only; do not levy on merchants at will."
translations.idiomatic: Xiū proposed: "Allow only the authorized lodge fees—no arbitrary taxes on merchants."

sentences.zh: 又：「收山澤寶冶，悉歸鹽鐵。」

translations.literal: Again: "Collect mountain, marsh, treasure, and smelting revenues—all to revert to salt and iron."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that revenues from mountains, marshes, mines, and smelters be centralized under the salt and iron bureau."

sentences.zh: 秉政凡五歲，罷為宣武軍節度使，封河東縣子。

translations.literal: Holding power altogether five years, he was dismissed to military commissioner of the Xuānwǔ Army and ennobled Viscount of Hédōng county.
translations.idiomatic: After five years in power he was sent out as commissioner of Xuānwǔ and ennobled as Viscount of Hédōng.

sentences.zh: 久之，由太子少保分司東都，復起歷昭義、河東、鳳翔、荊南四節度。

translations.literal: After a long while, from Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent he served at the Eastern Capital on detached duty; he was raised again and passed through the four commands of Zhāoyì, Hédōng, Fèngxiáng, and Jīngnán.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as junior tutor at the Eastern Capital, then returned to office and held four successive commands: Zhāoyì, Hédōng, Fèngxiáng, and Jīngnán.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十四，贈太尉。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-four; posthumously made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-four and was posthumously made grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 休不為察行，所治吏下畏信。

translations.literal: Xiū did not engage in minute surveillance of conduct; in every post he governed, clerks and subordinates feared and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiū did not nitpick his subordinates' conduct, yet in every post his staff feared and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 能文章，書楷遒媚有體法。

translations.literal: He could compose essays; his regular script was forceful and graceful with proper method.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote well, and his regular script was vigorous, elegant, and disciplined.

sentences.zh: 為人醞藉，進止雍閑。

translations.literal: As a man he was urbane; in advance and halt he was dignified and unhurried.
translations.idiomatic: Urbane in manner, he moved with dignified ease.

sentences.zh: 宣宗嘗曰：「休真儒者。」

translations.literal: Xuānzōng once said: "Xiū is a true Confucian."
translations.idiomatic: Xuānzōng once said, "Xiū is a true Confucian."

sentences.zh: 然嗜浮屠法，居常不禦酒肉，講求其說，演繹附著數萬言，習歌唄以為樂。

translations.literal: Yet he was addicted to Buddhist law; ordinarily he did not partake of wine or meat; he studied and sought its doctrines, elaborated and appended several myriad words, and practiced chanting hymns for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was devoted to Buddhism, abstained from wine and meat, wrote tens of thousands of words expounding the doctrine, and took his pleasure in chanting sutras.

sentences.zh: 與紇幹素善，至為桑門號以相字，當世嘲薄之，而所好不衰。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with the monk Gégān Sù, even to the point of taking monastic names as mutual courtesy names; the age mocked and slighted this, yet his fondness did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to the monk Gégān Sù, even exchanging monastic names as courtesy names—a habit contemporaries ridiculed, which he never gave up.

sentences.zh: 劉瑑，字子全，高宗宰相仁軌五世孫。

translations.literal: Liú Zhuàn, styled Zǐquán, was fifth-generation descendant of the Gāozōng grand councilor Rénkuǐ.
translations.idiomatic: Liú Zhuàn, courtesy name Zǐquán, was a fifth-generation descendant of Gāozōng's chancellor Rénkuǐ.

sentences.zh: 第進士，鎮國陳夷行表為判官。

translations.literal: He placed in the jinshi; Zhèngguó's Chén Yíxíng memorialized him as judge.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, and Chén Yíxíng of Zhèngguó appointed him as a staff judge.

sentences.zh: 入遷左拾遺，諫罷武宗方士，言多懇愊。

translations.literal: He entered and was transferred to Left Reminder; he remonstrated to abolish Wǔzōng's Daoist masters; his words were mostly earnest and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to left remonstrator, he urged Wǔzōng to dismiss his Daoist adepts in language both firm and sincere.

sentences.zh: 大中初，擢翰林學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dàzhōng he was selected as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dàzhōng he entered the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 宣宗始復關隴，裁處叢繁，書詔夜數十，雖捉筆遽成，辭皆允切。

translations.literal: When Xuānzōng began to recover Guān and Lǒng, decisions were piled and complex; imperial writs numbered dozens each night; though he took brush and finished hastily, the diction was all fitting and apt.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuānzōng began recovering the northwest, affairs piled up and edicts ran to dozens each night; Zhuàn drafted them at speed, yet every line was apt.

sentences.zh: 會伐党項，詔為行營宣慰使。

translations.literal: When they campaigned against the Dǎngxiàng, he was ordered as campaigning army consolation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against the Dǎngxiàng he was named campaigning consolation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部侍郎，乃裒匯敕令可用者，由武德訖大中，凡二千八百六十五事，類而析之，參訂重輕，號《大中刑律統類》以聞，法家推其詳。

translations.literal: Transferred to Vice Minister of Justice, he then gathered usable edicts and statutes from Wǔdé through Dàzhōng—altogether two thousand eight hundred sixty-five items—classified and analyzed them, compared and fixed severity and lightness, titled the Comprehensive Categories of the Dàzhōng Penal Code and submitted it; legalists praised its detail.
translations.idiomatic: As vice minister of justice he compiled 2,865 usable statutes and edicts from Wǔdé through Dàzhōng, classified them by topic, harmonized their penalties, and submitted the Comprehensive Categories of the Dàzhōng Penal Code, which jurists hailed for its thoroughness.

sentences.zh: 繇河南尹進宣武軍節度使。

translations.literal: From Jīngzhào Intendant he was advanced to military commissioner of the Xuānwǔ Army.
translations.idiomatic: From the capital intendant's post he was promoted to commissioner of Xuānwǔ.

sentences.zh: 先時，大饗雜進倡舞，彖曰：「豈軍中樂邪？」

translations.literal: Previously, at the great feast mixed entertainers and dancers were presented; Zhuàn said: "Is this army music?"
translations.idiomatic: At first the command held grand feasts with singers and dancers. Zhuàn asked, "Is this what an army should hear?"

sentences.zh: 取壯士千人，被鎧擁矛盾，習擊刺，與吏士臨觀。

translations.literal: He took a thousand stalwart men, clad in armor bearing spears and shields, practiced thrusting and stabbing, and had officials and soldiers observe.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered a thousand armored men with spear and shield, drilled them in combat, and made officers and troops watch.

sentences.zh: 又下令不訶止夜行，使民自便，境內以安。

translations.literal: He also ordered that night travel not be forbidden or stopped, letting the people go as they pleased; within the borders there was security.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted curfews so people could travel freely, and the circuit grew calm.

sentences.zh: 徙河東節度使。

translations.literal: Transferred to military commissioner of Hédōng.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hédōng.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以戶部侍郎召判度支。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue to oversee the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as vice minister of revenue to run the treasury.

sentences.zh: 始，瑑在翰林，帝素器遇。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhuàn was in the Hanlin, the emperor had always valued and treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long favored Zhuàn since his Hanlin days.

sentences.zh: 至是，手詔追還，外無知者，既發太原，人方大驚。

translations.literal: At this time, by autograph he was recalled; outside none knew; after he had set out from Tàiyuán, people were greatly startled.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor recalled him by autograph in secret. When he left Tàiyuán the court was astonished.

sentences.zh: 後請間，帝視案上歷，謂彖：「為朕擇一令日。」

translations.literal: Later he requested a private audience; the emperor looked at the calendar on the desk and said to Zhuàn: "Choose a good day for Us."
translations.idiomatic: At a later private audience the emperor studied the calendar and told Zhuàn, "Pick me an auspicious day."

sentences.zh: 瑑跪曰：「某日良。」

translations.literal: Zhuàn knelt and said: "Such-and-such a day is good."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuàn knelt and said, "That day is auspicious."

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「是日卿可遂相。」

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and said: "On that day you may complete your chancellorship."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled. "On that day you shall become my chancellor.

sentences.zh: 即詔同中書門下平章事，仍領度支。

translations.literal: He was at once ordered Associate Director and Grand Councilor, still overseeing the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: An edict at once named him grand councilor while he kept charge of revenue.

sentences.zh: 嘗與崔慎由議帝前，慎由請甄別流品，彖質曰：「王夷甫相晉，崇尚浮虛，以述流品，卒致淪夷。

translations.literal: Once he debated before the emperor with Cuī Shènyóu; Shènyóu asked to screen and classify pedigree ranks; Zhuàn rebutted: "Wáng Yífǔ served as Jin chancellor, exalting emptiness and vanity, and by narrating pedigree ranks in the end brought ruin on the Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Once, debating before the throne with Cuī Shènyóu, who urged sorting men by pedigree, Zhuàn replied: "When Wáng Yífǔ led Jin he exalted empty talk and ranked families by pedigree—and the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 今日不循名責實，使百吏各稱職，而先流品，未知所以致治也。」

translations.literal: Today, if we do not follow names and demand reality, making the hundred officials each fit his post, yet put pedigree ranks first, I do not know by what means to bring order."
translations.idiomatic: If today we do not match names to deeds and make every officer do his job, but put pedigree first, I see no path to good government."

sentences.zh: 慎由不得對，繇是罷宰相。

translations.literal: Shènyóu could not reply; from this he was dismissed as grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Shènyóu had no answer and was removed from the council.

sentences.zh: 俄而瑑大病，加工部尚書，拜臥內，猶手疏陳政事。

translations.literal: Before long Zhuàn fell gravely ill; he was given additional title Minister of Works; he was invested within the bedchamber, yet still by hand memorialized on government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuàn soon fell gravely ill. Promoted to minister of works, he received investiture at the bedside yet still drafted memorials on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 居位半歲卒，年六十三，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In office half a year he died at age sixty-three; posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died six months later at sixty-three and was posthumously made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 瑑以名節自將，凡議論處事不私，趨於當乃止，未嘗以言色借貴近。

translations.literal: Zhuàn took reputation and integrity as his guide; in every discussion and handling of affairs he was not partial; he proceeded until it was fitting and then stopped; he never lent words or countenance to the noble and near.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuàn held himself to reputation and integrity, argued and acted without favoritism, stopped when justice was done, and never softened his tone for the powerful.

sentences.zh: 與瑑同知政者夏侯孜。

translations.literal: Sharing power with Zhuàn was Xiàhóu Zī.
translations.idiomatic: His colleague on the council was Xiàhóu Zī.

sentences.zh: 孜，字好學，亳州譙人。

translations.literal: Zī, styled Hàoxué, was a man of Qiào in Bózhōu.
translations.idiomatic: Zī, courtesy name Hàoxué, came from Qiào in Bózhōu.

sentences.zh: 累遷婺、絳州刺史。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached governor of Wù and Jiàng.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to govern Wù and Jiàng prefectures.

sentences.zh: 繇兵部侍郎、諸道鹽鐵轉運使為同中書門下平章事，仍領鹽鐵。

translations.literal: From Vice Minister of War and commissioner of salt, iron, and transport for all circuits he became Associate Director and Grand Councilor, still heading salt and iron.
translations.idiomatic: From vice minister of war and head of salt, iron, and transport he became grand councilor while retaining the transport portfolio.

sentences.zh: 懿宗立，進門下侍郎、譙郡侯。

translations.literal: When Yìzōng acceded, he was advanced to Vice Director of the Chancellery and Marquis of Qiào commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Yìzōng came to the throne, Zī became vice director of the chancellery and Marquis of Qiào.

sentences.zh: 俄以同平章事出為西川節度使。

translations.literal: Before long, as Associate Director he went out as military commissioner of Western Chuān.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left the capital as grand councilor and commissioner of Western Chuān.

sentences.zh: 召拜尚書左僕射，還執政，進司空，為貞陵山陵使。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, he returned to hold power, was advanced to Minister of Works, and was made director for the Zhēnlíng mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as left vice director, he returned to power, rose to minister of works, and directed construction of Emperor Xuānzōng's mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 坐隧壞，出為河中節度使，猶同平章事。

translations.literal: Because the tunnel collapsed, he went out as military commissioner of Hézhōng, still Associate Director.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial tunnel collapsed he was sent to Hézhōng as commissioner, retaining his council title.

sentences.zh: 初，堂史署制，仆孜懷中，即死。

translations.literal: At first, a hall clerk was drafting an edict; he placed it in Zī's bosom, and at once died.
translations.idiomatic: Once a secretariat clerk drafting an edict slipped the draft into Zī's robe—and dropped dead on the spot.

sentences.zh: 不數日，孜罷。

translations.literal: Within a few days Zī was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Zī was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 咸通時，蠻犯蜀深入，士乏糧，追責孜治蜀無素備，以太子少保分司東都，卒。

translations.literal: In the Xián-tōng era, when the southern barbarians invaded Shǔ deeply, soldiers lacked grain; Zī was pursued and blamed for governing Shǔ without long-standing preparation; he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent on detached duty at the Eastern Capital, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiántōng, when Nanzhao raided deep into Shǔ and troops went hungry, the court blamed Zī for leaving Sichuan unprepared, demoted him to junior tutor at the Eastern Capital, and he died there.

sentences.zh: 趙隱，字大隱，京兆奉天人。

translations.literal: Zhào Yǐn, styled Dàyǐn, was a man of Fèngtiān in Jīngzhào.
translations.idiomatic: Zhào Yǐn, courtesy name Dàyǐn, came from Fèngtiān in the capital district.

sentences.zh: 祖植，當德宗出狩，變倉卒，羽衛單寡，朱泚攻城急，植率家人奴客以死拒守，獻家財勞軍，帝嘉之。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhí, when Dézōng went on campaign, the change was sudden; guards and escort were few and thin; Zhū Cī pressed the siege urgently; Zhí led family, household slaves, and retainers to resist unto death, presented family wealth to reward the army; the emperor praised it.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhí, when Dézōng fled the capital in haste with a thin guard, held his home against Zhū Cī's fierce siege with kin and retainers, gave his family wealth to the troops, and won the emperor's praise.

sentences.zh: 賊平，渾瑊引在幕府。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, Húnzhuǎn took him into the staff office.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion he entered Húnzhuǎn's staff.

sentences.zh: 累擢鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached governor of Zhèngzhōu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to governor of Zhèngzhōu.

sentences.zh: 鄭滑節度使李融奏以自副，融疾病，委以軍政。

translations.literal: Zhèng-Huá military commissioner Lǐ Róng memorialized to take him as deputy; when Róng fell ill, he entrusted him with military and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Lǐ Róng, commissioner of Zhèng and Huá, took him as deputy and, when illness struck, entrusted him with the command.

sentences.zh: 大將宋朝晏火其營，夜為亂，植列卒不動須之，遲明而潰，捕斬皆盡，優詔嘉慰。

translations.literal: The great general Sòng Cháoyàn set fire to the camp; at night there was disorder; Zhí arrayed troops unmoved and waited; toward dawn they dispersed; those captured were beheaded to the last; an excellent edict praised and comforted.
translations.idiomatic: When the general Sòng Cháoyàn burned the camp and mutiny broke out at night, Zhí held his ranks without stirring until dawn, when the rebels collapsed. The ringleaders were executed to a man, and the throne sent warm commendation.

sentences.zh: 累擢嶺南節度使，終於官。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached military commissioner of Lǐngnán and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually became commissioner of Lǐngnán and died in post.

sentences.zh: 父存約，辟署興元李絳府。

translations.literal: His father Cúnyuē was appointed to Lǐ Jiàng's staff in Xīngyuán.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cúnyuē served on Lǐ Jiàng's staff at Xīngyuán.

sentences.zh: 值軍亂，方與絳燕間，吏報賊至，絳麾存約使去，對曰：「荷公德厚，誼不當獨免。」

translations.literal: When army disorder arose, just as he was feasting with Jiàng, an official reported the bandits had come; Jiàng waved Cúnyuē to leave; he replied: "I have received your great virtue—righteousness does not permit me to escape alone."
translations.idiomatic: During a mutiny, as he feasted with Jiàng, word came that rebels were approaching. Jiàng urged him to flee; Cúnyuē answered, "You have shown me great kindness—I cannot save myself alone."

sentences.zh: 即部勒左右捍之，而同被害。

translations.literal: He at once marshaled his attendants to defend; together they were killed.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied his guards to resist and perished with Jiàng.

sentences.zh: 隱以父死難，與兄騭廬墓幾十年，闔門誦書，不應辟召。

translations.literal: Yǐn, because his father died in calamity, with his elder brother Zhì dwelt by the tomb in a hut for nearly ten years; the whole household recited books and did not answer recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death in the crisis, Yǐn and his elder brother Zhì mourned at the tomb for nearly ten years, the household studying together and refusing every summons.

sentences.zh: 親友更敦勉令仕，會昌中，擢進士第，歷州刺史、河南尹。

translations.literal: Kinsmen and friends repeatedly urged and exhorted him to take office; in Huìchāng he was selected in the jinshi degree; he passed through governor of a prefecture and Jīngzhào Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives finally persuaded him to serve; in Huìchāng he passed the jinshi, became a prefectural governor, and then capital intendant.

sentences.zh: 以兵部侍郎領鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: As Vice Minister of War he headed salt, iron, and transport.
translations.idiomatic: As vice minister of war he headed salt, iron, and transport.

sentences.zh: 咸通末，進同中書門下平章事，遷中書侍郎，封天水縣伯。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiántōng he was advanced to Associate Director and Grand Councilor, transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat, and ennobled Baron of Tiānshuǐ county.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xiántōng he became grand councilor and vice director of the secretariat, and was ennobled Baron of Tiānshuǐ.

sentences.zh: 性仁悌，不敢以貴權自處。

translations.literal: By nature he was benevolent and brotherly; he did not dare to comport himself by noble power.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and dutiful by nature, he never threw his rank about.

sentences.zh: 始布衣時，家無貲，與騭同耕以養，雖姻宗之富，未嘗幹以財。

translations.literal: When he was first a commoner, the family had no wealth; with Zhì he plowed together to support themselves; though affinal clans were rich, he never importuned them for money.
translations.idiomatic: As a commoner he was poor and farmed with Zhì to support the family, never asking wealthy in-laws for help.

sentences.zh: 宦浸顯，還家，易衣侍左右，猶布衣也。

translations.literal: As his office gradually became eminent and he returned home, he changed clothes to attend at left and right, yet was still like a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Even after high office, when he came home he changed into plain clothes to wait on his mother as a farmer's son.

sentences.zh: 騭終宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: Zhì ended as observation commissioner of Xuān and Shè.
translations.idiomatic: Zhì ended his career as commissioner of Xuān and Shè.

sentences.zh: 既輔政，它宰相及百官皆詣第升堂慶母，歲時公卿必參訊。

translations.literal: Once he assisted in government, other grand councilors and the hundred officials all came to his residence and ascended the hall to congratulate his mother; at year's seasons the public ministers invariably paid calls.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power, fellow councilors and officials called at his home to congratulate his mother, and ministers visited her every season.

sentences.zh: 懿宗誕日，宴慈恩寺，隱侍母以安輿臨觀，宰相方率百官拜恩於廷，即回班候夫人起居，搢紳以為榮。

translations.literal: On Yìzōng's birthday they feasted at Cí'ēn Temple; Yǐn attended his mother in a palanquin to observe; the grand councilors were just leading the hundred officials to bow in gratitude in the court; they then returned in formation to wait on the lady's health; gentry and officials regarded it as glory.
translations.idiomatic: On Yìzōng's birthday, at a feast in Cí'ēn Temple, Yǐn brought his mother in a palanquin while the council led officials in court obeisance, then the whole cohort waited on her health—a ritual the elite took as supreme honor.

sentences.zh: 後崔顏昭、張浚當國，皆有母，遂踵其禮。

translations.literal: Later Cuī Yánzhāo and Zhāng Jùn held the state; both had mothers; they then followed this rite.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Cuī Yánzhāo and Zhāng Jùn held power, each with a living mother, they copied the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 僖宗初，罷為鎮海軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xīzōng he was dismissed to military commissioner of the Zhènhǎi Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xīzōng's reign he was sent out as commissioner of Zhènhǎi.

sentences.zh: 王郢之亂，坐撫禦失宜，下除太常卿。

translations.literal: In Wáng Yǐng's disorder, because pacification and defense were improper, he was demoted to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After Wáng Yǐng's rebellion he was demoted for mishandling the crisis, reduced to minister of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 廣明初，為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guǎngmíng he was Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Guǎngmíng he was minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 居母喪，卒。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his mother, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died while mourning his mother.

sentences.zh: 子光逢、光裔、光胤，皆第進士，歷臺省華劇。

translations.literal: His sons Guāngféng, Guāngyì, and Guāngyìn all placed in the jinshi and passed through lofty posts in the censorate and secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Guāngféng, Guāngyì, and Guāngyìn all passed the jinshi and rose to eminent posts in the censorate and secretariat.

sentences.zh: 光逢尤規矱自持，以中書舍人為翰林學士。

translations.literal: Guāngféng especially measured and restrained himself; as Secretariat Drafter he became Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Guāngféng was the most self-disciplined; from secretariat drafter he entered the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 時光裔由膳部郎中知制誥，對掌內外命書，士歆羨之。

translations.literal: At the time Guāngyì, from Director in the Ceremonials Section, was drafting edicts; together they controlled inner and outer command documents; scholars admired and envied them.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Guāngyì drafted edicts as a director in the ministry of rites, so the brothers held inner and outer drafting between them—a feat scholars envied.

sentences.zh: 裴坦，字知進，隋營州都督世節裔孫。

translations.literal: Pei Tǎn, styled Zhījìn, was descendant of Suí's Yíngzhōu area commander Shìjié.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Tǎn, courtesy name Zhījìn, descended from the Suí area commander Shìjié of Yíngzhōu.

sentences.zh: 父乂，福建觀察使。

translations.literal: His father Yì was Fújiàn observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yì was commissioner of Fújiàn.

sentences.zh: 坦及進士第，沈傳師表置宣州觀察府，召拜左拾遺、史館修撰。

translations.literal: Tǎn placed in the jinshi degree; Shěn Chuánshī memorialized to place him in the Xuānzhōu observation office; summoned and appointed Left Reminder and historiography compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Tǎn passed the jinshi; Shěn Chuánshī placed him on the Xuānzhōu staff; he was recalled as left remonstrator and historiography compiler.

sentences.zh: 歷楚州刺史。

translations.literal: He passed through governor of Chǔzhōu.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Chǔzhōu.

sentences.zh: 令狐當國，薦為職方郎中，知制誥，而裴休持不可，不能奪。

translations.literal: When Líng Hú held the state, he recommended him as Director in the Board of Appointments and drafting edicts, but Pei Xiū firmly held it could not be done and could not be overborne.
translations.idiomatic: When Líng Hú dominated the court he recommended Tǎn as appointments director and edict drafter, but Pei Xiū firmly objected and could not be overruled.

sentences.zh: 故事，舍人初詣省視事，四丞相送之，施一榻堂上，壓角而坐。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a drafter first went to the Secretariat to take up affairs, four chief ministers escorted him; they placed one couch in the hall and sat pressing its corners.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, when a Secretariat drafter first reported to the Secretariat to assume his duties, four chancellors would escort him in; a couch would be set up in the hall, and all would sit each on a corner of it.

sentences.zh: 坦見休，重愧謝，休勃然曰：「此令狐丞相之舉，休何力？」

translations.literal: Tǎn saw Xiū and repeatedly apologized in shame; Xiū erupted: "This was Chancellor Líng Hú's doing — what strength had Xiū?
translations.idiomatic: When Tǎn went to see Xiū and bowed again and again in apology, Xiū flushed with anger and said, "This was Chancellor Líng Hú's appointment — what had I to do with it?

sentences.zh: 顧左右索肩輿亟出，省吏眙駭，以為唐興無有此辱，人為坦羞之。

translations.literal: He turned to those about him to seek a shoulder-sedan chair and hurried out; Secretariat clerks stared in shock, thinking that since Táng's founding there had never been such disgrace, and people felt shame for Tǎn.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to his attendants for a sedan chair and left at once. The Secretariat staff stood gaping, holding that nothing like this humiliation had occurred since the dynasty was founded; many felt embarrassment on Tǎn's behalf.

sentences.zh: 再進禮部侍郎，拜江西觀察使、華州刺史。

translations.literal: Again advanced to Vice Minister of Rites, appointed Jiāngxī observation commissioner and governor of Huázhōu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to vice minister of rites, then appointed commissioner of Jiāngxī and governor of Huá Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，不數月卒。

translations.literal: Summoned as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs with the Grand Councilor title; within a few months he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice director of the Secretariat and grand councilor; he died within a few months.

sentences.zh: 坦性簡儉，子娶楊收女，賫具多飾金玉，坦命撤去，曰：「亂我家法。」

translations.literal: Tǎn's nature was plain and frugal; his son married the daughter of Yáng Shōu; the dowry items were much adorned with gold and jade; Tǎn ordered them removed, saying: "You are disordering our family norms.
translations.idiomatic: Tǎn was spare and frugal by nature. When his son married Yáng Shōu's daughter, the bridal outfit was lavish with gold and jade. Tǎn had it stripped away, saying, "This overturns the way of our household.

sentences.zh: 世清其概。

translations.literal: The world prized his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries admired his principled bearing.

sentences.zh: 從子贄。

translations.literal: His collateral nephew Zhì.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Zhì.

sentences.zh: 贄，字敬臣，及進士第，擢累右補闕、御史中丞、刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Zhì, styled Jìngchén, placed in the jinshi degree; promoted through Right Reminder, Censor-in-Chief, and Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhì, courtesy name Jìngchén, passed the jinshi examination and rose through the posts of right-reminder, censor-in-chief, and vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 昭宗引拜中書侍郎兼本官、同中書門下平章事，尋兼戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhāozōng led him in to be appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat while retaining his original post and made Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs with the Grand Councilor title; soon he also held the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhāozōng personally invested him as vice director of the Secretariat while retaining his existing rank, made him grand councilor, and shortly thereafter added minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝疑其外風檢而匿帷薄，逮問翰林學士韓偓，偓曰：「贄，咸通大臣坦從子，內雍友，合疏屬以居，故臧獲猥眾，出入無度，殆此致謗言者。」

translations.literal: The emperor suspected that outwardly he showed moral restraint but concealed improprieties within the women's apartments; he summoned and asked Hanlin academician Hán Wō; Wō said: "Zhì is collateral nephew of Tǎn, a great minister of Xiántōng; inwardly he is harmonious and friendly; one ought to have distant kin lodge with him, therefore slaves and servants were many and vulgar, comings and goings without measure — probably this brought on slander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected that Zhì maintained an upright public manner while hiding domestic misconduct. He questioned Hanlin academician Hán Wō, who replied: "Zhì is the nephew of Tǎn, a senior minister from the Xiántōng reign. He is warm-hearted at home and ought to have had more distant relatives living with him; instead his household was crowded with riffraff whose comings and goings knew no bounds — that is likely what drew the gossip.

sentences.zh: 帝每聞咸通事，必肅然斂衽，故偓稱之為贄地。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor heard of Xiántōng affairs, he would solemnly straighten his robe; therefore Wō called it "Zhì ground."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor heard matters from the Xiántōng era, he would compose himself and straighten his robes; hence Wō called such topics "Zhì territory."

sentences.zh: 帝幸鳳翔，為大明宮留守，罷。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Fèngxiáng, Zhì served as custodian of the Daming Palace, then was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Fengxiang, Zhì was left as warden of Daming Palace and later removed.

sentences.zh: 俄進尚書左僕射，以司空致仕。

translations.literal: Soon advanced to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, retiring as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to left vice director of the Secretariat and retired with the title minister of works.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠將篡，貶青州司戶參軍，殺之。

translations.literal: As Zhū Quánzhōng was about to usurp, Zhì was demoted to army adjutant of Qīngzhōu and killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhū Quánzhōng was poised to seize the throne, Zhì was demoted to registrar of Qingzhou and executed.

sentences.zh: 鄭延昌，字光遠，咸通末，得進士第，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: Zhèng Yánchāng, styled Guāngyuǎn, at the end of Xiántōng placed in the jinshi degree, moved up to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhèng Yánchāng, courtesy name Guāngyuǎn, passed the jinshi at the close of Xiántōng and became an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 鄭畋鎮鳳翔，表在其府。

translations.literal: When Zhèng Tián commanded Fèngxiáng, he memorialized to have Yánchāng in his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhèng Tián held Fengxiang, he had Yánchāng appointed to his staff.

sentences.zh: 黃巢亂京師，畋倚延昌調兵食，且諭慰諸軍。

translations.literal: When Huáng Cháo threw the capital into chaos, Tián relied on Yánchāng to regulate troops and provisions and also instructed and comforted the armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Huáng Cháo ravaged the capital, Tián relied on Yánchāng to manage troops and supplies and to reassure the various armies.

sentences.zh: 畋再秉政，擢司勛員外郎、翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Tián again held power, Yánchāng was raised to Outer Adjunct in the Ministry of Personnel and Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Tián returned to office, he promoted Yánchāng to an outer adjunct in the Ministry of Personnel and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 進累兵部侍郎，兼京兆尹判度支。

translations.literal: Advanced through successive offices to Vice Minister of War, also Intendant of Jīngzhào while judging the Treasury Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of war, concurrently serving as metropolitan intendant of the capital while overseeing the treasury.

sentences.zh: 拜戶部尚書，以中書侍郎同中書門下平章事，兼刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Appointed Minister of Revenue; as Vice Director of the Secretariat made Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs with the Grand Councilor title, also holding the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister of revenue, then vice director of the Secretariat and grand councilor, with the additional title of minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 無它功，以病罷，拜尚書左僕射，卒。

translations.literal: Without other achievement, removed on account of illness, appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Having accomplished little else, he was removed because of illness, named left vice director of the Secretariat, and died.

sentences.zh: 王溥，字德潤，失其何所人。

translations.literal: Wáng Pǔ, styled Déyùn — his place of origin is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Wáng Pǔ, courtesy name Déyùn, was a man whose native place is unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 第進士，擢累禮部員外郎、史館脩撰。

translations.literal: Placed in the jinshi degree, promoted through Outer Adjunct of the Ministry of Rites and compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and rose through outer adjunct in the Ministry of Rites and compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 崔胤鎮武安，表署觀察府判官。

translations.literal: When Cuī Yìn commanded Wǔ'ān, he memorialized to appoint Pǔ administrative judge of the observation office.
translations.idiomatic: When Cuī Yìn took command of Wǔ'ān, he had Pǔ appointed administrative aide in his observation staff.

sentences.zh: 胤不赴鎮，溥留充集賢殿直學士。

translations.literal: Yìn did not go to his posting; Pǔ remained to fill a direct academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Yìn never went to his post, and Pǔ stayed on as a direct academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞趙光逢奏為刑部郎中，知雜事。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Zhào Guāngféng memorialized to make him Langzhong of the Ministry of Justice, managing miscellaneous matters.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Zhào Guāngféng had him appointed a director in the Ministry of Justice with charge of assorted bureau business.

sentences.zh: 昭宗蒙難東內，溥與胤說衛軍執劉季述等殺之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhāozōng suffered hardship in the Eastern Inner Palace, Pǔ together with Yìn persuaded the palace guard to seize Liú Jìshù and others and kill them.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Zhāozōng was besieged in the eastern inner palace, Pǔ and Yìn persuaded the imperial guards to seize Liú Jìshù and his faction and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 帝反正，驟拜翰林學士、戶部侍郎，以中書侍郎同中書門下平章事，判戶部。

translations.literal: When the emperor was restored, Pǔ was suddenly appointed Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Revenue; as Vice Director of the Secretariat he became Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs with the Grand Councilor title and judged the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor was restored, Pǔ was swiftly made Hanlin academician and vice minister of revenue, then vice director of the Secretariat, grand councilor, and overseer of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 不能有所裨益，罷為太子賓客，分司東部。

translations.literal: Unable to offer any benefit, he was dismissed to Guest of the Heir Apparent with detached duty in the Eastern Office.
translations.idiomatic: Finding he could be of little use, the court removed him to honorary mentor of the heir with a nominal post in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召拜太常卿、工部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long summoned and appointed Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as minister of imperial sacrifices and minister of works.

sentences.zh: 會朱溫侵逼，貶淄州司戶參軍，賜自盡，與裴樞等投屍於河。

translations.literal: When Zhū Wēn pressed his aggression, Pǔ was demoted to army adjutant of Zīzhōu, granted suicide, and with Pei Shū and others his corpse was cast into the river.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhū Wēn tightened his grip, Pǔ was demoted to registrar of Zī Prefecture and ordered to take his own life; his body, like those of Pei Shū and the others, was thrown into the river.

sentences.zh: 盧光啟，字子忠，不詳何所人。

translations.literal: Lú Guāngqǐ, styled Zǐzhōng — it is not known whence he came.
translations.idiomatic: Lú Guāngqǐ, courtesy name Zǐzhōng, was a man whose origins are unknown.

sentences.zh: 第進士，為張浚所厚，擢累兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Placed in the jinshi degree, favored by Zhāng Jùn, promoted through to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi graduate, he won Zhāng Jùn's favor and rose to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 昭宗幸鳳翔，宰相皆不從，以光啟權總中書事，兼判三司，進左諫議大夫，參知機務。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhāozōng visited Fèngxiáng, the chancellors all did not follow; Guāngqǐ was empowered to oversee Secretariat affairs temporarily, also judged the Three Commissions, advanced to Left Aide to the Censorate, and assisted in state secrets.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhāozōng fled to Fengxiang and none of the chancellors went with him, Guāngqǐ was left to handle Secretariat business provisionally, also oversee the three treasury offices; he was promoted to left remonstrating aide and given a role in deliberations on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 復拜兵部侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Again appointed Vice Minister of War and Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs with the Grand Councilor title.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed vice minister of war and grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 俄罷為太子少保，改吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon dismissed to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, changed to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon removed to junior mentor of the heir, then transferred to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 初，光啟執政，韋貽範、蘇檢相繼為宰相。

translations.literal: At the outset, when Guāngqǐ held power, Wéi Yífàn and Sū Jiǎn in succession became chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during Guāngqǐ's tenure, Wéi Yífàn and Sū Jiǎn each in turn became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 貽範，字垂憲，以龍州刺史貶通州，檢為洋州刺史。

translations.literal: Yífàn, styled Chuíxiàn, from governor of Lóngzhōu was demoted to Tōngzhōu; Jiǎn was governor of Yángzhōu.
translations.idiomatic: Yífàn, courtesy name Chuíxiàn, had been demoted from governor of Longzhou to Tongzhou; Jiǎn had served as governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二人奔行在，貽範遷給事中。

translations.literal: The two fled to the mobile court; Yífàn was transferred to Supervising Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Both men rushed to join the emperor on campaign; Yífàn was promoted to supervising drafter.

sentences.zh: 用李茂貞薦，閱旬為工部侍郎、同中書門下平章事，判度支。

translations.literal: By Lǐ Màozhēn's recommendation, within ten days he was Vice Minister of Works, Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs with the Grand Councilor title, judging the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: On Lǐ Màozhēn's recommendation, within ten days he became vice minister of works, grand councilor, and overseer of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 倚權臣，恣驁不恭。

translations.literal: Relying on powerful ministers, he acted wildly without respect.
translations.idiomatic: Backed by men in power, he behaved arrogantly and without deference.

sentences.zh: 會母喪免，逾月奪服。

translations.literal: Meeting his mother's mourning he was excused; after a month mourning garb was seized back.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he left office for mourning, but a month later he was recalled from bereavement by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 不數月卒。

translations.literal: Within a few months he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died within a few months.

sentences.zh: 檢初拜中書舍人，貽範薦於茂貞，即拜工部侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Jiǎn at first was appointed Secretariat Drafter; Yífàn recommended him to Màozhēn, and he was immediately made Vice Minister of Works and Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs with the Grand Councilor title.
translations.idiomatic: Jiǎn had first been made a Secretariat drafter; Yífàn commended him to Màozhēn, and he was at once named vice minister of works and grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 茂貞與朱全忠通好，乃求尚主，取檢女為景王妃以固恩。

translations.literal: Màozhēn was on friendly terms with Zhū Quánzhōng; therefore he sought to marry an imperial princess, taking Jiǎn's daughter as consort to the Prince of Jǐng to solidify favor.
translations.idiomatic: On good terms with Zhū Quánzhōng, Màozhēn sought an imperial marriage alliance and took Jiǎn's daughter as wife for the Prince of Jǐng to cement their bond.

sentences.zh: 帝還京師，檢長流環州，光啟賜死。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital, Jiǎn was banished by long exile to Huánzhōu; Guāngqǐ was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to Chang'an, Jiǎn was sentenced to distant exile in Huanzhou, and Guāngqǐ was ordered to take his own life.
